# Skill Author

Helps you write **new agent skills** that follow the best-practices documented at
https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/ — without you having to re-read those pages
every time. Pairs with `skill-creator` (which handles eval/iterate/optimize loops
once a draft exists).

## When to use this vs `skill-creator`

| Task | Use |
|---|---|
| "I want to make a new skill for X" | **skill-author** (scaffold + author) |
| "Scaffold the SKILL.md / a reference / a script" | **skill-author** |
| "Lint this skill draft" | **skill-author** |
| "My skill isn't triggering when I want it to" | `skill-creator` (description optimization) |
| "Run test cases against my skill, benchmark it" | `skill-creator` (eval loop) |
| "Compare two versions of my skill" | `skill-creator` (blind comparison) |

If both apply, start here, then hand off to `skill-creator` once the draft is solid.

## Workflow

### 1. Capture intent (1 minute)

Before scaffolding, get four answers — usually just by asking the user:

1. **What does it do?** (one sentence)
2. **When should it trigger?** (specific user phrases / contexts)
3. **What does it output?** (file, command result, plan, prose)
4. **Is the output objectively verifiable?** (decides whether `skill-creator` evals are worth the effort later)

Write these four down before touching files. They become the seeds for the
description, the workflow body, and the future eval set.

### 2. Scaffold

Use `scripts/new-skill.sh` to produce the directory layout. The script
auto-detects **scope** (where to put the skill) and fans out discovery
symlinks for non-universal agents so the skill is loadable immediately.

```bash
bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh <skill-name>
```

Three scopes (auto-detected; override with `--local` / `--project` / `--global`):

| Scope | Canonical dir | Symlinks created |
|---|---|---|
| **LOCAL** (this publishing repo: vendor.yaml / skills/local/ found walking up) | `<repo>/skills/local/<name>/` (or `skills/vendor/<name>/` with `--vendor`) | `.agents/skills/<name>` + `.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../skills/{local,vendor}/<name>` |
| **PROJECT** (inside another git repo) | `<repo>/.agents/skills/<name>/` (universal agents — Cursor / Codex / OpenCode / Warp — pick this up directly) | `.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../.agents/skills/<name>` (+ any already-present non-universal agent dir at the repo root) |
| **GLOBAL** (no git repo found) | `~/.agents/skills/<name>/` | `~/.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../.agents/skills/<name>` (+ any detected non-universal agent dir under `$HOME`) |

The template's frontmatter has placeholders that lint will reject — this is on
purpose so the agent can't forget to fill them in.

> **Important**: When the user's intent is ambiguous (they're inside a git repo
> but haven't said whether the skill should live with the project or be
> available everywhere), **ask** "system-wide (`--global`) or just this
> project (`--project`)?" before running the script. The script is
> non-interactive — once you've picked a scope, files land and symlinks fan
> out without further prompting.

After running, the script emits a single JSON object on stdout with
`{skill, mode, canonical, symlinks[], next_steps[]}` so you can chain
follow-up actions deterministically.

### 3. Author the SKILL.md

Read `references/authoring-patterns.md` before writing the body. The patterns
that matter most:

- **Description must be "pushy"** and include concrete trigger contexts. Naive
  descriptions cause undertriggering — the #1 failure mode of new skills. Keep
  this within the cross-agent budget: 120-500 chars is the preferred range,
  501-900 is valid but context-heavy, 901-1024 is valid but close to hard
  loader limits, and >1024 is invalid for Codex/Cursor/spec-aligned skills.
- **Gotchas section** — environment-specific facts that defy reasonable
  assumptions. The single highest-value section in most skills.
- **Output templates** — agents pattern-match against concrete structures more
  reliably than they follow prose descriptions of formats.
- **Calibrated specificity** — be prescriptive only where the task is fragile;
  give the agent freedom (and explain *why*) where multiple approaches are valid.
- **Defaults, not menus** — pick one tool/approach and mention alternatives as
  escape hatches.

Keep `SKILL.md` under 500 lines. If you blow past that, move detail into
`references/<topic>.md` and tell the agent **when** to load it ("Read X if Y
happens"), not just that it exists.

### 4. Design any scripts

Before writing a script, read `references/script-design.md`. Skills script
design is meaningfully different from "regular" CLI script design because the
caller is an LLM reading your stderr to decide what to do next. The non-obvious
requirements:

- No interactive prompts, ever (agents run in non-interactive shells)
- `--help` is the primary interface documentation — keep it concise but complete
- Errors must say *what was expected* and *what to try*, not just *what failed*
- Structured stdout (JSON/CSV/TSV), prose diagnostics to stderr — separate them
- `--dry-run` for any destructive operation
- Pin versions for `uvx` / `npx` / `pipx` invocations

For Python helpers, prefer **PEP 723 inline dependencies** + `uv run` over
`requirements.txt` — the script becomes self-contained and the agent doesn't
have to set up an environment first.

### 5. Lint

Run the linter before committing or handing off to `skill-creator`:

```bash
bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/lint-skill.sh skills/local/<skill-name>
```

It checks three things:

1. **Frontmatter & length** — `name` and `description` exist; name is
   hyphen-case and <=64 chars; description has a "use when" trigger phrase,
   respects the 1024-char hard limit, and SKILL.md is under 500 lines.
2. **Script hygiene** — every `scripts/*.sh` has a shebang, is executable, and
   responds to `--help` (presence of the flag handler, not necessarily a working
   script).
3. **Reference reachability** — every file in `references/` is mentioned at
   least once from `SKILL.md` (no dead reference docs).

Fix every error. Warnings are advisory but usually worth addressing.

### 6. (Optional) Hand off to skill-creator

Once lint passes and the skill *looks* right, the next questions are
quantitative: does it trigger reliably? does it produce good output? That's
`skill-creator` territory. Tell the user: "skill-author got the structure
right. If you want to validate it works on real prompts, the `skill-creator`
skill runs test cases and benchmarks."

## Available scripts

- **`scripts/new-skill.sh <name>`** — Scaffold the canonical skill dir
  (SKILL.md, references/, scripts/, assets/) and add discovery symlinks for
  non-universal agents. Auto-detects scope (LOCAL / PROJECT / GLOBAL); see
  table in step 2.
  - Scope flags (mutually exclusive): `--local` (force this repo's
    `skills/local/`), `--project` (force `<repo>/.agents/skills/`),
    `--global` (force `~/.agents/skills/`).
  - Other flags: `--vendor` (LOCAL only — `skills/vendor/<name>/` instead of
    `skills/local/`; rare, vendored skills normally come via `vendor.yaml`);
    `--root DIR` (override walk-up); `--no-symlinks` (skip the fan-out);
    `--dry-run`; `--force` (overwrite existing canonical dir + replace
    symlinks).
- **`scripts/lint-skill.sh <skill-dir>`** — Run frontmatter, script hygiene,
  and reference reachability checks. Exit non-zero on any error.
  - Flags: `--strict` (treat warnings as errors); `--quiet` (only print failures).

## Bundled assets

Templates that `new-skill.sh` copies and that you can reference manually:

- `assets/SKILL.md.template` — Frontmatter + workflow skeleton with placeholders.
- `assets/reference.md.template` — Reference doc skeleton (TOC + sections).
- `assets/script-bash.template` — Bash 3.2 compatible script with `set -euo pipefail`,
  `--help` / `--dry-run` flag handler, structured-output friendly logging
  (data → stdout, prose → stderr).
- `assets/script-python.template` — Python script with PEP 723 inline-deps
  block, argparse with help/examples, dry-run support.

## Reference files

- `references/authoring-patterns.md` — The agentskills.io "best practices"
  page condensed: gotchas, templates, validation loops, calibrated specificity,
  defaults-not-menus, procedures-over-declarations, plan-validate-execute.
- `references/script-design.md` — The agentskills.io "using scripts" page
  condensed: agentic CLI design, structured output, error message style,
  PEP 723, uvx/npx/pipx version pinning, dry-run patterns.
- `references/this-repo-conventions.md` — Conventions specific to *this*
  repository: where to put local vs vendor skills, how the 5-level skill
  search works, AGENTS.md ↔ CLAUDE.md sync, where mirrored scripts live.

## Gotchas

- **AGENTS.md is a symlink to CLAUDE.md** — edit either one; never replace the
  symlink with a real file.
- **Skill discovery is one level deep first, then recursive up to 5 levels.**
  `skills/local/<name>/SKILL.md` works because of the recursive fallback. Don't
  nest skills more than 5 deep or they become invisible.
- **`bash 3.2` compatibility** is required for any script that might run on
  stock macOS. No `mapfile`, no `${var,,}` lowercasing, no `[[ -v var ]]`.
  See `references/script-design.md` for the safe subset.
- **`description` is always-on context and has agent-specific hard limits.**
  Put concrete trigger phrases in frontmatter, but keep local skills in the
  120-500 char preferred range when possible. Treat >1024 chars as invalid:
  Codex and Cursor/spec-aligned validators can skip the skill entirely.
- **Don't write a skill that wraps something the agent already does well.**
  If a stock Claude session handles the task in one turn without help, a skill
  adds context-window cost for no gain. Test the no-skill baseline before
  investing in authoring.
- **Scope auto-detect can surprise you.** `new-skill.sh` walks up looking for
  a publishing-repo anchor (`vendor.yaml` / `skills/local/` /
  `skills/.claude-plugin/`) *first*, then a `.git`. If you ran it from inside
  a clone of this repo while meaning to add a skill to your *other* project,
  it'll silently land in `skills/local/`. Pass `--project` or `--global`
  explicitly when intent isn't obvious, and prefer asking the user
  system-wide-vs-project-wide before running.
- **Discovery symlinks must be `../../`-relative**, not repo-root-relative —
  POSIX resolves symlink targets relative to the link's own directory. The
  script enforces this and verifies each link with `test -e <link>/SKILL.md`;
  if you ever hand-create one, see
  [`pitfalls/symlink-target-relative-to-symlink-not-cwd.md`](../../../pitfalls/symlink-target-relative-to-symlink-not-cwd.md).

## When the user is updating an existing skill (not creating new)

Same workflow, but skip step 2 (scaffold). Read the existing SKILL.md first,
identify which patterns from `references/authoring-patterns.md` are missing or
weakly applied, and propose edits one section at a time so the user can sanity
check. After edits, run lint, then offer the `skill-creator` handoff for
quantitative validation.

Once lint passes and the skill *looks* right, the next questions are
quantitative: does it trigger reliably? does it produce good output? That's
`skill-creator` territory. Tell the user: "skill-author got the structure
right. If you want to validate it works on real prompts, the `skill-creator`
skill runs test cases and benchmarks."

## Available scripts

- **`scripts/new-skill.sh <name>`** — Scaffold the canonical skill dir
  (SKILL.md, references/, scripts/, assets/) and add discovery symlinks for
  non-universal agents. Auto-detects scope (LOCAL / PROJECT / GLOBAL); see
  table in step 2.
  - Scope flags (mutually exclusive): `--local` (force this repo's
    `skills/local/`), `--project` (force `<repo>/.agents/skills/`),
    `--global` (force `~/.agents/skills/`).
  - Other flags: `--vendor` (LOCAL only — `skills/vendor/<name>/` instead of
    `skills/local/`; rare, vendored skills normally come via `vendor.yaml`);
    `--root DIR` (override walk-up); `--no-symlinks` (skip the fan-out);
    `--dry-run`; `--force` (overwrite existing canonical dir + replace
    symlinks).
- **`scripts/lint-skill.sh <skill-dir>`** — Run frontmatter, script hygiene,
  and reference reachability checks. Exit non-zero on any error.
  - Flags: `--strict` (treat warnings as errors); `--quiet` (only print failures).

## Bundled assets

Templates that `new-skill.sh` copies and that you can reference manually:

- `assets/SKILL.md.template` — Frontmatter + workflow skeleton with placeholders.
- `assets/reference.md.template` — Reference doc skeleton (TOC + sections).
- `assets/script-bash.template` — Bash 3.2 compatible script with `set -euo pipefail`,
  `--help` / `--dry-run` flag handler, structured-output friendly logging
  (data → stdout, prose → stderr).
- `assets/script-python.template` — Python script with PEP 723 inline-deps
  block, argparse with help/examples, dry-run support.

## Reference files

- `references/authoring-patterns.md` — The agentskills.io "best practices"
  page condensed: gotchas, templates, validation loops, calibrated specificity,
  defaults-not-menus, procedures-over-declarations, plan-validate-execute.
- `references/script-design.md` — The agentskills.io "using scripts" page
  condensed: agentic CLI design, structured output, error message style,
  PEP 723, uvx/npx/pipx version pinning, dry-run patterns.
- `references/this-repo-conventions.md` — Conventions specific to *this*
  repository: where to put local vs vendor skills, how the 5-level skill
  search works, AGENTS.md ↔ CLAUDE.md sync, where mirrored scripts live.

## Gotchas

- **AGENTS.md is a symlink to CLAUDE.md** — edit either one; never replace the
  symlink with a real file.
- **Skill discovery is one level deep first, then recursive up to 5 levels.**
  `skills/local/<name>/SKILL.md` works because of the recursive fallback. Don't
  nest skills more than 5 deep or they become invisible.
- **`bash 3.2` compatibility** is required for any script that might run on
  stock macOS. No `mapfile`, no `${var,,}` lowercasing, no `[[ -v var ]]`.
  See `references/script-design.md` for the safe subset.
- **`description` is always-on context and has agent-specific hard limits.**
  Put concrete trigger phrases in frontmatter, but keep local skills in the
  120-500 char preferred range when possible. Treat >1024 chars as invalid:
  Codex and Cursor/spec-aligned validators can skip the skill entirely.
- **Don't write a skill that wraps something the agent already does well.**
  If a stock Claude session handles the task in one turn without help, a skill
  adds context-window cost for no gain. Test the no-skill baseline before
  investing in authoring.
- **Scope auto-detect can surprise you.** `new-skill.sh` walks up looking for
  a publishing-repo anchor (`vendor.yaml` / `skills/local/` /
  `skills/.claude-plugin/`) *first*, then a `.git`. If you ran it from inside
  a clone of this repo while meaning to add a skill to your *other* project,
  it'll silently land in `skills/local/`. Pass `--project` or `--global`
  explicitly when intent isn't obvious, and prefer asking the user
  system-wide-vs-project-wide before running.
- **Discovery symlinks must be `../../`-relative**, not repo-root-relative —
  POSIX resolves symlink targets relative to the link's own directory. The
  script enforces this and verifies each link with `test -e <link>/SKILL.md`;
  if you ever hand-create one, see
  [`pitfalls/symlink-target-relative-to-symlink-not-cwd.md`](../../../pitfalls/symlink-target-relative-to-symlink-not-cwd.md).

## When the user is updating an existing skill (not creating new)

Same workflow, but skip step 2 (scaffold). Read the existing SKILL.md first,
identify which patterns from `references/authoring-patterns.md` are missing or
weakly applied, and propose edits one section at a time so the user can sanity
check. After edits, run lint, then offer the `skill-creator` handoff for
quantitative validation.

包含我個人習慣也會把 .vscode/{settings,extensions}.json 等 checkin 目的是在新的地方拉起來就能有一樣的dev環境等等

# Usage: make add-todo ARGS="--priority P3 --effort M --title 'X' --description 'Y'"
add-todo:
	./scripts/add-todo.sh $(ARGS)

# Usage: make promote-todo ARGS="--title 'substring' --summary 'shipped summary'"
promote-todo:
	./scripts/promote-todo.sh $(ARGS)

sweep-inbox:
	./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh $(ARGS)

# Docs site: MkDocs Material + mkdocs-llmstxt + mkdocs-copy-to-llm.
# Requires `uv sync --extra docs` once.
docs-serve:
	uv run mkdocs serve

docs-build:
	uv run mkdocs build

# Manual one-shot deploy (CI handles this on push to main).
docs-deploy:
	uv run mkdocs gh-deploy --force

# Test the agent-history-hygiene skill: pytest (unit + corpus) + bash
# exit-code contract. Requires `uv sync --extra dev` once, plus
# `gitleaks` on PATH for the corpus + shell tests (they skip gracefully
# if missing).
test-skill:
	uv run --extra dev pytest skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/tests/ -q
	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/tests/test_scan_staged.sh
```
</details></tool-use>

32	die()  { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }
33	
34	DRY_RUN=0
35	ARGS=()
36	
37	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
38	  case "$1" in
39	    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
40	    --help|-h) usage; exit 0 ;;
41	    --) shift; while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do ARGS+=("$1"); shift; done ;;
42	    -*) die "unknown flag: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
43	    *)  ARGS+=("$1"); shift ;;
44	  esac
45	done
46	
47	if [ "${#ARGS[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
48	  die "missing required argument (try --help)" 1
49	fi
50	
51	main() {
52	  local target="${ARGS[0]}"
53	  log "Processing: $target"
54	
55	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
56	    log "[dry-run] Would do work on: $target"
57	    return 0
58	  fi
59	
60	  # Real work goes here. Emit structured data on stdout.
61	  printf '{"target":"%s","status":"ok"}\n' "$target"
62	}
63	
64	main
65
```

```text
1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Validate skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json — the catalog manifest
3	# read by `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`.
4	#
5	# Checks:
6	#   1. JSON parses
7	#   2. `name` is not on the official reserved list
8	#   3. Every plugins[].skills[] path exists and contains SKILL.md
9	#   4. No skill path is listed under more than one plugin
10	#   5. (warn) Every on-disk SKILL.md under skills/ is either listed in
11	#      some plugin or will fall through to "Other" in the picker UI.
12	#
13	# Errors (1-4) exit non-zero; (5) is warn-only so the build doesn't break
14	# while a skill is mid-add.
15	#
16	# Reference: docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md
17	set -euo pipefail
18	
19	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
20	SKILLS_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/skills"
21	MANIFEST="$SKILLS_DIR/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json"
22	
23	RED='\033[0;31m'
24	GREEN='\033[0;32m'
25	YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
26	NC='\033[0m'
27	
28	errors=0
29	warnings=0
30	
31	err()  { printf "${RED}ERROR:${NC} %s\n"   "$*" >&2; errors=$((errors+1)); }
32	warn() { printf "${YELLOW}WARN:${NC}  %s\n" "$*" >&2; warnings=$((warnings+1)); }
33	ok()   { printf "${GREEN}OK:${NC}    %s\n"  "$*"; }
34	
35	# 1. File exists + valid JSON
36	if [[ ! -f "$MANIFEST" ]]; then
37	  err "manifest not found: $MANIFEST"
38	  exit 1
39	fi
40	if ! jq empty "$MANIFEST" 2>/dev/null; then
41	  err "manifest is not valid JSON: $MANIFEST"
42	  exit 1
43	fi
44	ok "JSON parses"
45	
46	# 2. Marketplace name is not reserved.
47	# Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces (reserved names section).
48	RESERVED=(
49	  claude-code-marketplace
50	  claude-code-plugins
51	  claude-plugins-official
52	  anthropic-marketplace
53	  anthropic-plugins
54	  agent-skills
55	  knowledge-work-plugins
56	  life-sciences
57	)
58	name="$(jq -r '.name // ""' "$MANIFEST")"
59	if [[ -z "$name" ]]; then
60	  err "manifest has no top-level 'name' field"
61	fi
62	for r in "${RESERVED[@]}"; do
63	  if [[ "$name" == "$r" ]]; then
64	    err "marketplace name '$name' is on the reserved list"
65	  fi
66	done
67	[[ $errors -eq 0 ]] && ok "marketplace name '$name' is not reserved"
68	
69	# 3. Every plugins[].skills[] path exists with a SKILL.md.
70	# Skills paths are relative to the manifest directory ($SKILLS_DIR).
71	declare -A seen_paths=()
72	duplicates=0
73	while IFS=$'\t' read -r plugin_name skill_path; do
74	  # Resolve relative to skills/
75	  resolved="$SKILLS_DIR/${skill_path#./}"
76	  if [[ ! -d "$resolved" ]]; then
77	    err "plugin '$plugin_name': directory not found: $skill_path  (resolved: $resolved)"
78	    continue
79	  fi
80	  if [[ ! -f "$resolved/SKILL.md" ]]; then
81	    err "plugin '$plugin_name': missing SKILL.md in $skill_path"
82	    continue
83	  fi
84	  if [[ -n "${seen_paths[$skill_path]+x}" ]]; then
85	    err "duplicate skill path '$skill_path' (also under plugin '${seen_paths[$skill_path]}')"
86	    duplicates=$((duplicates+1))
87	  else
88	    seen_paths[$skill_path]="$plugin_name"
89	  fi
90	done < <(jq -r '.plugins[] | .name as $n | .skills[]? | [$n, .] | @tsv' "$MANIFEST")
91	
92	listed_count=${#seen_paths[@]}
93	ok "$listed_count skill paths listed; all exist with SKILL.md"
94	[[ $duplicates -eq 0 ]] && ok "no duplicate skill paths across plugins"
95	
96	# 4. (already covered by duplicates check above)
97	
98	# 5. Warn for on-disk skills not covered by any plugin (will fall under "Other").
99	# Discovery: depth 2 (skills/<top>/<name>/SKILL.md) + depth 3 (skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/SKILL.md).
100	on_disk_paths=$(
101	  find "$SKILLS_DIR" -maxdepth 4 -name SKILL.md -not -path '*/.claude-plugin/*' \
102	    | sed "s|^$SKILLS_DIR/||; s|/SKILL.md\$||" \
103	    | sort
104	)
105	unlisted=0
106	while IFS= read -r rel; do
107	  [[ -z "$rel" ]] && continue
108	  key="./$rel"
109	  if [[ -z "${seen_paths[$key]+x}" ]]; then
110	    warn "skill '$rel' not listed in any plugin — will appear under 'Other'"
111	    unlisted=$((unlisted+1))
112	  fi
113	done <<< "$on_disk_paths"
114	
115	if [[ $unlisted -eq 0 ]]; then
116	  ok "all on-disk skills are covered by a plugin (no fallback to 'Other')"
117	fi
118	
119	echo
120	if [[ $errors -gt 0 ]]; then
121	  printf "${RED}FAILED${NC}: %d error(s), %d warning(s)\n" "$errors" "$warnings" >&2
122	  exit 1
123	fi
124	printf "${GREEN}PASSED${NC}: 0 errors, %d warning(s)\n" "$warnings"
125
```
</details></tool-use>

1	# Adding catalog entries
2	
3	How to add or update entries in the [Catalog](../catalog/index.md) —
4	new external skills, new MCP servers, new domain hubs, or status
5	changes on existing entries.
6	
7	This workflow couples the catalog to `vendor.yaml` and `TODO.md` (the
8	existing sources of truth) without duplicating them. Catalog pages are
9	the *vendoring decision log*; the actual vendoring happens via existing
10	scripts.
11	
12	## When to write a catalog entry
13	
14	| You discovered… | Where it goes | Status to start with |
15	|---|---|---|
16	| An external skill you might want to vendor | [`skill-collections.md`](../catalog/skill-collections.md) + relevant [domain hub](../catalog/domains/index.md) | `wishlist` |
17	| An MCP server you want to remember | New file under [`catalog/mcp/`](../catalog/mcp/index.md) + relevant domain hub | `wishlist` |
18	| A whole new professional domain | New file under [`catalog/domains/`](../catalog/domains/index.md) (copy `_template.md`) | (hub itself, not entry) |
19	| A skill you looked at and rejected | Add to `skill-collections.md` with reason | `skipped` |
20	| A skill you looked at but didn't decide on | Add to `skill-collections.md` with 1-line note | `evaluated` |
21	
22	## Status enum
23	
24	--8<-- "_snippets/external-install.md"
25	
26	## Status change recipes
27	
28	### `wishlist` → `deferred`
29	
30	The entry has crossed into "we should evaluate this" territory.
31	
32	```bash
33	./scripts/add-todo.sh --priority P? --effort <S|M|L> \
34	  --title "<skill-name> skill" \
35	  --description "Evaluate <upstream URL> for <use case>. See catalog/<page>.md."
36	```
37	
38	Then edit the catalog entry: change `status: wishlist` → `status: deferred`,
39	link to the new TODO line.
40	
41	### `deferred` → `vendored`
42	
43	The entry has been evaluated and we want to vendor it.
44	
45	```bash
46	# Vendor the skill (writes to vendor.yaml + downloads files)
47	./scripts/add-vendor.sh <owner>/<repo>/<path-to-skill>
48	
49	# Or with a series subdir
50	./scripts/add-vendor.sh --series <series-name> <owner>/<repo>/<path-to-skill>
51	
52	# If the entry had a TODO P? line, promote it
53	./scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" \
54	  --summary "Vendored from <upstream URL>"
55	```
56	
57	Then edit the catalog entry: change `status: deferred` → `status: vendored`,
58	update the link to point at `skills/vendor/<name>/` (or
59	`skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/`).
60	
61	### `wishlist` / `evaluated` → `skipped`
62	
63	You read the upstream and decided not to vendor.
64	
65	Just edit the catalog entry: change status → `skipped`, add the reason
66	inline (one sentence). Examples:
67	
68	- "Skipped — duplicates `<other-skill>` from `<more-authoritative-source>`."
69	- "Skipped — Slack-specific; not portable."
70	- "Skipped — narrower than `<existing-local-skill>` and overlaps it."
71	
72	## Adding a new MCP entry
73	
74	1. Create `docs/catalog/mcp/<slug>.md` with the YAML frontmatter
75	   schema documented in [`mcp/index.md`](../catalog/mcp/index.md#per-entry-conventions).
76	2. Fill the 6-section body (TL;DR / capabilities / install / when /
77	   related / sources).
78	3. Translate to `docs/catalog/mcp/<slug>.zh-TW.md`.
79	4. Add to the `mkdocs.yml` nav under `Catalog → MCP wiki`.
80	5. Add a row to the entries table in
81	   [`mcp/index.md`](../catalog/mcp/index.md).
82	6. Cross-link from any relevant domain hub's MCP section.
83	
84	When the MCP wiki has 5+ entries, the index table will be regenerated
85	by a script (planned — see follow-up TODOs). Until then, edit the
86	table by hand.
87	
88	## Adding a new domain hub
89	
90	See the [How to add a new domain hub](../catalog/domains/index.md#how-to-add-a-new-domain-hub)
91	section in the Domains overview — the recipe lives next to the
92	template it references.
93	
94	## Bilingual obligation
95	
96	Every page in `docs/catalog/` (except the snippet and `_template.md`)
97	must have a `*.zh-TW.md` counterpart. The `mkdocs-i18n` plugin's
98	`fallback_to_default: true` means missing translations don't break the
99	build, but the project convention is that every published page has
100	both languages in the same PR.
101	
102	## Validation
103	
104	```bash
105	make docs-build       # strict mode catches missing snippets / broken links
106	make marketplace      # ensure no regression on vendor.yaml / marketplace.json
107	make kanban           # ensure TODO.md still parses
108	```
109	
110	Open the served site (`make docs-serve`) and click through the new
111	entries' cross-links to verify they resolve.
112
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# TODO format
2	
3	This page documents the exact grammar that
4	[`scripts/todo-kanban.sh`](scripts.md#todo-kanbansh) validates. It applies
5	to this repo's own [`TODO.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/blob/main/TODO.md)
6	and to any project that has run
7	[`project-knowledge-harness`'s `init.sh`](../skills/project-knowledge-harness.md).
8	
9	## File-level structure
10	
11	1. The first non-empty heading **must** be `# TODO`.
12	2. Sections **must** appear in this order:
13	   `## P1`, `## P2`, `## P3`, `## P?`, `## Done`.
14	3. After `## Done`, additional `## ...` headings are allowed (e.g. a
15	   `## Notes` section, a prune log). The validator stops checking item
16	   format at that point.
17	4. Anything that is **not** a top-level `- [ ]` / `- ✅` item — prose
18	   paragraphs, blockquotes, HTML comments, `---` rules, indented
19	   sub-bullets — is ignored. You can write inline guidance under each
20	   section heading without breaking validation.
21	
22	## Item-level grammar
23	
24	| Lane | Format |
25	|---|---|
26	| `P1` / `P2` / `P3` | `- [ ] **[Effort] Title** — description` |
27	| `P?` | `- [ ] **[?/Effort] Title** — description` |
28	| `Done` | `- ✅ [YYYY-MM-DD] [P#/Effort] Title — summary` |
29	
30	Where:
31	
32	- **Effort** is one of `S`, `M`, `L`, `XL`. For `P?` items where effort
33	  is also unknown, use `[?/?]`.
34	- **Title** must not contain `*` (the validator uses the closing `**` as
35	  a delimiter).
36	- **Description / summary** can be free text after the em-dash
37	  (`—`, U+2014). Plain hyphens (`-`) are not accepted.
38	- Active items may end with ` → [research](backlog/<slug>.md)` to link
39	  the index entry to a `backlog/` doc.
40	- `Done` items use a date in `YYYY-MM-DD` format. UTC by convention; the
41	  promote script uses `date -u +%Y-%m-%d`.
42	
43	## Examples
44	
45	```markdown
46	## P1
47	
48	- [ ] **[S] Wire up GitHub Pages** — first deploy of the docs site
49	
50	## P2
51	
52	- [ ] **[L] Migrate kanban to Python** — Bash 3.2 compat is getting expensive → [research](backlog/kanban-python.md)
53	
54	## P?
55	
56	- [ ] **[?/M] Try Rspress for docs** — evaluate AI-native docs framework alternative
57	- [ ] **[?/?] Skill-set lint** — vague idea, needs scoping
58	
59	## Done
60	
61	- ✅ [2026-04-23] [P1/M] Restructure project-knowledge-harness — looser validator, init/promote scripts, references/ progressive disclosure
62	```
63	
64	## Tools that depend on this format
65	
66	- [`scripts/todo-kanban.sh`](scripts.md#todo-kanbansh) — validator and
67	  Markdown / JSON board renderer.
68	- [`scripts/promote-todo.sh`](scripts.md#promote-todosh) — atomic move
69	  from active lane to `## Done`.
70	- [`scripts/add-todo.sh`](scripts.md#add-todosh) — structured insert into
71	  the right lane.
72	- [`scripts/sweep-inbox.sh`](scripts.md#sweep-inboxsh) — formalize loose
73	  captures from `backlog/inbox.md` via repeated `add-todo.sh` calls.
74	
75	If you find yourself wanting a syntax that isn't here, it's worth asking
76	whether the new shape is genuinely useful or whether it's another
77	`IDEAS.md` file in disguise — see
78	[`references/anti-patterns.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/references/anti-patterns.md).
79
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# Authoring patterns
2	
3	Condensed from <https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/best-practices>. Read this
4	before writing or editing a SKILL.md body.
5	
6	## Table of contents
7	
8	1. [Spending context wisely](#spending-context-wisely)
9	2. [Cross-agent frontmatter compatibility](#cross-agent-frontmatter-compatibility)
10	3. [Calibrating control](#calibrating-control)
11	4. [Gotchas sections](#gotchas-sections)
12	5. [Output templates](#output-templates)
13	6. [Checklists for multi-step workflows](#checklists-for-multi-step-workflows)
14	7. [Validation loops](#validation-loops)
15	8. [Plan-validate-execute](#plan-validate-execute)
16	9. [Bundling reusable scripts](#bundling-reusable-scripts)
17	10. [Quick checklist before commit](#quick-checklist-before-commit)
18	
19	---
20	
21	## Spending context wisely
22	
23	Every token in `SKILL.md` competes with the conversation history, the system
24	prompt, and every other active skill. Spend tokens on what the agent **wouldn't
25	know without you**:
26	
27	- Project-specific conventions (table names, repo layout, internal jargon)
28	- Domain-specific procedures with non-obvious steps
29	- Edge cases the agent will misjudge by default
30	- Specific tools/APIs to prefer (with the *why*, briefly)
31	
32	Don't spend tokens on:
33	
34	- Explaining what well-known things are (PDF, HTTP, REST, JSON)
35	- Generic "best practices" the agent already applies (handle errors, write tests)
36	- Comprehensive option enumerations — give a default and one escape hatch
37	
38	**Test:** for each paragraph, ask "would the agent get this wrong without it?"
39	If no, cut it.
40	
41	### Progressive disclosure
42	
43	Three loading levels:
44	
45	| Level | Loaded | Budget |
46	|---|---|---|
47	| Frontmatter (`name`, `description`) | always | 120-500 chars preferred, 1024 max |
48	| `SKILL.md` body | when skill triggers | <500 lines, <5000 tokens |
49	| `references/*.md`, `assets/*`, `scripts/*` | on demand | unlimited |
50	
51	If `SKILL.md` is creeping past 500 lines, move sections to `references/<topic>.md`
52	and reference them with **load conditions** ("Read X if Y happens"), not just
53	"see X for details". Conditions let the agent load on demand; bare pointers tend
54	to either get ignored or get pre-loaded out of caution.
55	
56	---
57	
58	## Cross-agent frontmatter compatibility
59	
60	Use this as the portable baseline for coding agents that consume Agent Skills:
61	
62	- `name`: required, lowercase letters/digits/hyphens only, no leading/trailing
63	  hyphen, no `--`, <=64 characters.
64	- `description`: required, non-empty string, <=1024 characters. Include both
65	  what the skill does and concrete trigger contexts. Keep the first 60
66	  characters meaningful because `npx skills` truncates picker hints there.
67	- Keep `name` and `description` as the only required frontmatter fields for
68	  portability. Agent-specific fields are allowed when needed, but isolate them
69	  intentionally: Cursor uses `disable-model-invocation`, Codex can read
70	  `agents/openai.yaml`, and some vendored skills carry upstream-only metadata.
71	
72	Description budget tiers:
73	
74	| Tier | Length | Meaning |
75	|---|---:|---|
76	| Green | 120-500 chars | Preferred for local skills: enough trigger surface without context bloat |
77	| Yellow | 501-900 chars | Valid, but context-heavy; move details to `SKILL.md` body |
78	| Orange | 901-1024 chars | Valid, but close to hard loader limits |
79	| Red | >1024 chars | Invalid for Codex/Cursor/spec-aligned validators |
80	
81	Agent notes:
82	
83	- **Codex** skips invalid `SKILL.md` files; OpenAI's validator enforces the
84	  64-char name and 1024-char description limits.
85	- **Cursor** managed `create-skill` guidance matches the same 64/1024 limits
86	  and supports `disable-model-invocation` for explicit-only skills.
87	- **Claude Code** uses descriptions for discovery and tolerates additional
88	  frontmatter in practice, but long descriptions still consume always-on
89	  context and are poor picker hints.
90	- **OpenCode** follows the Agent Skills convention and uses descriptions for
91	  invocation; stay within the portable baseline unless a target agent's docs
92	  say otherwise.
93	- **Claude.ai upload** may impose stricter UI limits. Treat that as a separate
94	  packaging target, not the default coding-agent baseline for this repo.
95	
96	---
97	
98	## Calibrating control
99	
100	Match instruction specificity to **task fragility**, not to "we should be thorough".
101	
102	### Be prescriptive when:
103	
104	- The operation is destructive or has side effects
105	- A specific sequence of steps must hold (migration, release, deploy)
106	- An external system requires exact format (API contract, parser input)
107	
108	```markdown
109	## Database migration
110	
111	Run exactly this sequence:
112	
113	    python scripts/migrate.py --verify --backup
114	
115	Do not modify the command or add flags. The `--verify` step seeds an
116	integrity check that later phases depend on.
117	```
118	
119	The trailing sentence is the trick — even when prescriptive, **explain why**.
120	Agents that understand the reason follow it more reliably than agents that just
121	see "DO NOT" in caps.
122	
123	### Give the agent freedom when:
124	
125	- Multiple valid approaches exist
126	- The output is judgment-driven (code review, refactor proposal)
127	- You'd be hand-coding policy if you wrote it all out
128	
129	```markdown
130	## Code review process
131	
132	1. Check database queries for SQL injection (use parameterized queries)
133	2. Verify auth checks on every endpoint
134	3. Look for race conditions in concurrent code paths
135	4. Confirm error messages don't leak internals
136	```
137	
138	Notice: *what to look for*, not *how to look for it*. The agent picks the
139	approach.
140	
141	### Defaults, not menus
142	
143	When several tools could work, pick one default and mention alternatives as
144	escape hatches.
145	
146	```markdown
147	Use pdfplumber for text extraction.
148	
149	For scanned PDFs requiring OCR, fall back to pdf2image with pytesseract.
150	```
151	
152	…not:
153	
154	```markdown
155	You can use pypdf, pdfplumber, PyMuPDF, or pdf2image depending on...
156	```
157	
158	### Procedures over declarations
159	
160	Teach the agent *how* to approach the class of problem, not *what* to produce
161	for one instance.
162	
163	```markdown
164	Bad — only useful for this exact query:
165	  Join `orders` to `customers` on `customer_id`, filter region='EMEA',
166	  sum `amount`.
167	
168	Good — works for any query:
169	  1. Read schema from `references/schema.yaml` to find relevant tables.
170	  2. Join via the `_id` foreign key convention.
171	  3. Apply user-requested filters as WHERE clauses.
172	  4. Aggregate numeric columns and format as a markdown table.
173	```
174	
175	Specifics still belong in the skill (output format templates, "never output
176	PII", tool-specific quirks) — but the *approach* should generalize.
177	
178	---
179	
180	## Gotchas sections
181	
182	Often the single highest-value section in a skill. **Concrete corrections to
183	mistakes the agent will make without being told.** Not generic advice.
184	
185	```markdown
186	## Gotchas
187	
188	- The `users` table uses soft deletes. Queries must include
189	  `WHERE deleted_at IS NULL` or results will include deactivated accounts.
190	- The user ID is `user_id` in the database, `uid` in the auth service, and
191	  `accountId` in the billing API. All three refer to the same value.
192	- The `/health` endpoint returns 200 if the web server is up, even if the
193	  database is down. Use `/ready` to check full service health.
194	```
195	
196	Keep gotchas in `SKILL.md`, not in a separate reference. The whole point is
197	that the agent reads them **before** hitting the situation — by the time it
198	realizes it should load `references/gotchas.md`, the bug has happened.
199	
200	**Iteration tip:** every time you correct the agent during a real run, add the
201	correction here. Most skills' gotchas sections grow over weeks, not get written
202	all at once.
203	
204	---
205	
206	## Output templates
207	
208	Agents pattern-match against concrete structures more reliably than they
209	follow prose descriptions. When the output has a fixed shape, paste the shape:
210	
211	````markdown
212	## Report structure
213	
214	Use this template, adapting sections as needed:
215	
216	```markdown
217	# [Analysis Title]
218	
219	## Executive summary
220	[One paragraph]
221	
222	## Key findings
223	- Finding 1 with supporting data
224	- Finding 2 with supporting data
225	
226	## Recommendations
227	1. Specific actionable recommendation
228	2. Specific actionable recommendation
229	```
230	````
231	
232	Long templates or templates that only apply in some cases should live in
233	`assets/<name>.template` and be loaded on demand from `SKILL.md`.
234	
235	---
236	
237	## Checklists for multi-step workflows
238	
239	Make dependencies and validation gates visible:
240	
241	```markdown
242	## Form processing workflow
243	
244	Progress:
245	- [ ] 1. Analyze the form  → `scripts/analyze_form.py`
246	- [ ] 2. Create field mapping  → edit `fields.json`
247	- [ ] 3. Validate mapping  → `scripts/validate_fields.py`
248	- [ ] 4. Fill the form  → `scripts/fill_form.py`
249	- [ ] 5. Verify output  → `scripts/verify_output.py`
250	```
251	
252	The agent treats the checkboxes as state and won't skip to step 4 without
253	ticking 1-3. Dependency arrows make the wiring explicit.
254	
255	---
256	
257	## Validation loops
258	
259	For tasks where output quality is testable, instruct the agent to validate
260	and re-try, not "do your best and stop":
261	
262	```markdown
263	## Editing workflow
264	
265	1. Make your edits.
266	2. Run validation: `python scripts/validate.py output/`
267	3. If validation fails:
268	   - Read the error message.
269	   - Fix the issues.
270	   - Run validation again.
271	4. Only proceed when validation passes.
272	```
273	
274	The validator can be a script, a reference checklist, or a self-check prompt.
275	The pattern is identical: **do → validate → fix → re-validate → proceed**.
276	
277	---
278	
279	## Plan-validate-execute
280	
281	For batch or destructive operations, force the agent through an intermediate
282	**plan artifact** that gets validated before any side effects happen:
283	
284	```markdown
285	## PDF form filling
286	
287	1. Extract form fields:
288	   `python scripts/analyze_form.py input.pdf`  → `form_fields.json`
289	2. Create `field_values.json` mapping each field name to its intended value.
290	3. Validate:
291	   `python scripts/validate_fields.py form_fields.json field_values.json`
292	   (checks every field exists, types match, required fields present)
293	4. If validation fails, revise `field_values.json` and re-validate.
294	5. Fill the form:
295	   `python scripts/fill_form.py input.pdf field_values.json output.pdf`
296	```
297	
298	The magic is step 3. A validator that catches "field 'signature_date' not
299	found — available: customer_name, order_total, signature_date_signed" lets the
300	agent self-correct **before** the destructive step 5.
301	
302	This pattern eliminates an entire class of "oops, ran the wrong thing on prod"
303	failures. Use it any time the actual operation is hard to undo.
304	
305	---
306	
307	## Bundling reusable scripts
308	
309	When you iterate on a skill (with `skill-creator`), watch the agent transcripts
310	across test runs. If the agent independently reinvents the same logic each run
311	— building the same chart, parsing the same format, validating the same way —
312	that's a signal to write the script once and bundle it in `scripts/`.
313	
314	Heuristic: if you see the same ~20-line helper appearing in 2+ runs, bundle it.
315	
316	See `references/script-design.md` for **how** to design bundled scripts so an
317	agent can call them reliably.
318	
319	---
320	
321	## Quick checklist before commit
322	
323	Before considering a SKILL.md "done":
324	
325	- [ ] Description includes specific trigger contexts ("use when X, Y, Z"),
326	      not just a one-line summary
327	- [ ] Description is "pushy" but within budget: 120-500 chars preferred,
328	      <=1024 chars required
329	- [ ] First 60 description chars are useful in picker UIs
330	- [ ] Name is hyphen-case and <=64 chars
331	- [ ] SKILL.md is under 500 lines (move overflow into `references/`)
332	- [ ] Every `references/*.md` is mentioned with a load condition, not just
333	      listed at the bottom
334	- [ ] Has a `## Gotchas` section (or an honest reason it's empty)
335	- [ ] Output format, if structured, is shown as a literal template
336	- [ ] Multi-step procedures use checklists with dependencies marked
337	- [ ] Destructive operations go through plan-validate-execute or have
338	      `--dry-run` support
339	- [ ] Bundled scripts are listed under `## Available scripts` with their flags
340	- [ ] No "MUST" / "ALWAYS" / "NEVER" in caps without an accompanying *why*
341
```

```text
1	# This-repo conventions
2	
3	Conventions specific to the `daviddwlee84/agent-skills` repository. Skills
4	authored elsewhere may follow different rules; this file is the source of
5	truth for **this** repo.
6	
7	## Layout
8	
9	```
10	skills/
11	├── local/             # skills authored in this repo (committed in full)
12	│   └── <skill-name>/
13	│       ├── SKILL.md
14	│       ├── references/
15	│       ├── scripts/
16	│       └── assets/
17	└── vendor/            # skills cherry-picked from upstream repos
18	    └── <skill-name>/
19	        └── ...        # synced via scripts/sync-vendor.sh
20	```
21	
22	- **New skills authored here go in `skills/local/`.** Always.
23	- **Don't manually edit anything in `skills/vendor/`** — it gets overwritten by
24	  the next `make sync`. Upstream changes go through `vendor.yaml` + `make sync`.
25	- **`.agents/skills/` and `.claude/skills/` at the repo root are active
26	  discovery-symlink farms**, not legacy. Each entry under them is a relative
27	  symlink (`../../skills/local/<name>` or `../../skills/vendor/<name>`) so
28	  that Cursor / Codex / Warp / OpenCode (`.agents/skills/`) and Claude Code
29	  (`.claude/skills/`) can dogfood the skills authored in this repo. The
30	  `new-skill.sh` scaffolder creates these symlinks automatically in **LOCAL
31	  mode**; never add new *canonical* skill content directly under them here.
32	
33	## `new-skill.sh` placement scopes
34	
35	`scripts/new-skill.sh` supports three placement scopes that mirror the
36	behavior of `npx skills add` (`vercel-labs/skills`). Auto-detection
37	precedence (when no flag given):
38	
39	1. **LOCAL** — publishing-repo anchor (`vendor.yaml`, `skills/local/`, or
40	   `skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`) found walking up. This is the
41	   default *inside this very repo*. Canonical content lives in
42	   `<repo>/skills/local/<name>/` (or `skills/vendor/<name>/` with
43	   `--vendor`); the script adds the `.agents/skills/` + `.claude/skills/`
44	   discovery symlinks for you.
45	2. **PROJECT** — a git root found walking up. Canonical content goes to
46	   `<repo>/.agents/skills/<name>/` (universal agents like Cursor / Codex /
47	   OpenCode / Warp / Gemini-CLI / Copilot read this directly); a relative
48	   symlink `<repo>/.claude/skills/<name> -> ../../.agents/skills/<name>` is
49	   added for Claude Code, plus links for any other non-universal agent dir
50	   (e.g. `.windsurf/`, `.continue/`) that already exists at the repo root.
51	3. **GLOBAL** — neither anchor found, or `--global` forced. Same shape as
52	   PROJECT but rooted at `$HOME`: canonical at `~/.agents/skills/<name>/`,
53	   plus `~/.claude/skills/<name>` and any other already-present
54	   `~/.<agent>/skills/` link.
55	
56	The fan-out rule is "claude-code always, others only if their config root
57	already exists at the base dir" — this mirrors `npx skills add`'s
58	"don't create `.windsurf/` unless the project already uses Windsurf"
59	behavior. The script never creates a new top-level agent home dir.
60	
61	Symlinks are always *relative* with a fixed `../../` prefix because both
62	the link's parent (`.../skills/`) and the canonical dir
63	(`.../.agents/skills/` or `.../skills/local/`) are exactly two levels under
64	the base dir. See [`pitfalls/symlink-target-relative-to-symlink-not-cwd.md`](../../../../pitfalls/symlink-target-relative-to-symlink-not-cwd.md)
65	for the historical bug this convention prevents.
66	
67	## Skill discovery
68	
69	The `skills` CLI looks for `SKILL.md` files like this:
70	
71	1. **First pass:** one level deep — `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`.
72	2. **Fallback:** recursive up to **5 levels** if first pass found nothing
73	   useful.
74	
75	That's why `skills/local/<name>/SKILL.md` and `skills/vendor/<name>/SKILL.md`
76	both work — they're 2 levels deep, well within the recursive fallback. **Don't
77	nest a skill more than 5 levels deep** or it becomes invisible.
78	
79	## Scripts naming and mirroring
80	
81	Some scripts are bundled into a skill **and** mirrored to `scripts/` at repo
82	root. The pattern:
83	
84	| Canonical location | Mirror |
85	|---|---|
86	| `skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/scripts/add-todo.sh` | `scripts/add-todo.sh` |
87	| `skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/scripts/sweep-inbox.sh` | `scripts/sweep-inbox.sh` |
88	| `skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/scripts/promote-todo.sh` | `scripts/promote-todo.sh` |
89	| `skills/local/project-knowledge-harness/scripts/todo-kanban.sh` | `scripts/todo-kanban.sh` |
90	
91	Reason: the canonical copy travels with the skill (downstream consumers get it
92	via `init.sh`). The root-level mirror is for *this* repo's own use so `make`
93	targets and CI don't have to know the skill's path.
94	
95	**Mirrors must stay byte-identical.** If you edit one, run the equivalent
96	`cp` to update the other and verify with `diff`. There is currently no
97	automated check for this — be careful.
98	
99	## Documentation
100	
101	- `README.md` — short repo entrypoint with install snippet.
102	- `docs/` — built into a MkDocs Material site at
103	  `https://daviddwlee84.github.io/agent-skills/`.
104	- `docs/skills/<skill-name>.md` — user-facing docs for each local skill. Link
105	  back to the canonical SKILL.md on GitHub via absolute URL (see linking rules
106	  in `docs/reference/docs-stack-recipe.md`).
107	
108	When you add a new local skill, also add:
109	
110	1. A row to `docs/skills/index.md`.
111	2. A `docs/skills/<skill-name>.md` page (can be short; cross-link to SKILL.md).
112	3. A nav entry in `mkdocs.yml`.
113	4. A row to the README's "What's in here" table.
114	
115	## Project memory
116	
117	This repo uses the `project-knowledge-harness` skill on itself. That means:
118	
119	- `TODO.md` is structured (P1/P2/P3/P?/Done sections, validated by
120	  `scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only`).
121	- `backlog/inbox.md` is the loose-capture inbox.
122	- `backlog/<slug>.md` holds research notes for non-trivial items.
123	- `pitfalls/<slug>.md` holds debugging traps with symptom-first titles.
124	
125	When authoring a skill, if you discover a non-obvious trap, write it to
126	`pitfalls/`. Don't bury it in commit messages or chat history.
127	
128	## AGENTS.md ↔ CLAUDE.md
129	
130	`AGENTS.md` is a **symlink** to `CLAUDE.md`. Edit either one. Don't replace
131	the symlink with a real file or they'll drift.
132	
133	## Bash compatibility
134	
135	All bundled scripts must be **bash 3.2 compatible** (stock macOS). See
136	`script-design.md` § "Bash 3.2 compatibility" for the safe subset and
137	escape hatches.
138	
139	## When this repo's conventions conflict with agentskills.io
140	
141	The agentskills.io best practices are upstream / generic; this file is local /
142	specific. When they conflict, this file wins **for skills authored in this
143	repo**. Notable specifics:
144	
145	- We default to bundling helper scripts in `scripts/` rather than relying on
146	  ad-hoc `uvx` invocations, because we want the helpers to compose with the
147	  repo's `Makefile` and CI.
148	- We use Bash for orchestration scripts (TODO management, vendor sync) so they
149	  run without a Python environment. PEP 723 Python is fine for analytical or
150	  parsing-heavy helpers.
151	- Skill descriptions in this repo lean **even pushier** than the agentskills.io
152	  guidance because we're optimizing for the OpenCode/Claude Code default
153	  triggering behavior, which under-triggers more aggressively than Claude.ai.
154

1	---

3	description: Commit SpecStory chat transcripts (`.specstory/history/*.md`), Claude Code plan files (`.claude/plans/*.md`, `plansDirectory`), and other coding-agent artifacts (`.cursor/plans/`, `.cursor/rules/`, `.opencode/plans/`, `.specify/`, `.codex/`) alongside the feature diff they produced — without leaking `.env` contents, API keys, or private-key PEM blocks into git history. Use when the user says "commit my chat", "save this specstory session", "stage the plan file", "scrub the transcript", "my .env leaked in chat", "bootstrap pre-commit for this project", or when you notice untracked `.specstory/history/*.md` or `.claude/plans/*.md` files while running `git status`. Also use after an accidental push of a secret to enforce rotate-first, rewrite-last remediation instead of reflexive `git push --force`.
4	---
5	
6	# agent-history-hygiene
7	
8	Keep agent chat transcripts and plan files committed together with the
9	code they produced, without leaking secrets. Pairs with the
10	`redact-agent-secrets` + `gitleaks` pre-commit hooks the skill installs.
11	
12	Three surfaces, separated by purpose:
13	
14	| Surface                          | Question it answers                                          |
15	|----------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|
16	| `find-session.sh`                | "Which transcript / plan file is *my* current session?"      |
17	| `stage-agent-artifacts.sh`       | "Which agent files belong in the next commit?"               |
18	| `bootstrap-project.sh`           | "How do I get pre-commit + gitleaks + redactor into a repo?" |
19	| `scan-staged.sh`                 | "Is there a leaked secret in what I'm about to commit?"      |
20	| `references/remediation.md`      | "I already pushed a secret — now what?"                      |
21	
22	## Core invariants
23	
24	1. **Agent transcripts and plan files are committed alongside the diff
25	   that produced them.** Never add them to `.gitignore`. An agent that
26	   drops these from a commit has broken the user's review trail.
27	2. **Rotate at the provider before any git rewrite.** The only act
28	   that revokes a leaked credential is rotation. History rewriting
29	   scrubs bytes on one clone and leaves them on every other.
30	3. **`git push --force` against a shared branch is never the fix for a
31	   leak.** At best it's useless; at worst it destroys teammate work and
32	   silently re-introduces the secret when someone merges their old
33	   history back.
34	
35	## When to use this skill
36	
37	Use it when the user (or you) surface any of:
38	
39	- "Commit my chat" / "save the specstory session" / "include the plan
40	  file in this commit" / "把 plan 跟 specstory 一起 commit 進去".
41	- You see dirty `.specstory/history/*.md`, `.claude/plans/*.md`,
42	  `.cursor/plans/*.md`, or any other configured agent artifact during
43	  `git status` and you're about to commit a feature.
44	- "Scrub this transcript" / "redact my key" / "gitleaks flagged my
45	  chat history".
46	- "Set up pre-commit for this repo" / "I'm starting a new project — how
47	  do I get the hook stack?" / "bootstrap secret scanning here".
48	- "I pushed a `.env`" / "a secret went to main" / "do I need to force
49	  push?" — the agent must steer to `references/remediation.md` and
50	  stop the user from force-pushing reflexively.
51	
52	## When NOT to use
53	
54	- The user explicitly wants agent transcripts **excluded** from the
55	  repo. Respect that; suggest a one-liner `.gitignore` addition and
56	  skip this skill entirely.
57	- The leak is already on a shared `main`/release branch. Do **not**
58	  offer to rewrite history — jump to `references/remediation.md` §5.
59	- The project genuinely has no agent session (no `.specstory/`, no
60	  `.claude/plans/`, etc.). Nothing to stage.
61	- Single-file, single-commit hygiene that the agent handles without any
62	  script (e.g., adding a missing trailing newline).
63	
64	## Integration with existing infrastructure
65	
66	This skill sits **on top of** any chezmoi-managed stack the user
67	already has. It does not duplicate:
68	
69	- **chezmoi's global `core.hooksPath`** (`~/.config/git/hooks/pre-commit`)
70	  — that wrapper runs the repo's `.pre-commit-config.yaml` and then
71	  optionally `gitleaks git --staged`. The skill bootstraps the repo-level
72	  config the wrapper expects to find.
73	- **chezmoi's `.gitleaks.toml`** — the user's config already carries
74	  curated rules for common API keys (OpenAI, Anthropic, Supabase,
75	  Linear, WakaTime, Cursor, HuggingFace, Notion, Tailscale, Clash /
76	  V2Ray tokens). The skill's `assets/gitleaks.toml.template` ships the
77	  same rule IDs so `.gitleaksignore` / allowlist tweaks stay portable.
78	- **the pinned `redact-agent-secrets` hook** — the redactor ships as a
79	  pinned pre-commit hook from this repo
80	  (`.pre-commit-hooks.yaml`), so every consuming repo gets fixes via
81	  `pre-commit autoupdate` instead of a vendored copy that drifts. Details
82	  in [`references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`](references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md).
83	
84	What this skill **adds**:
85	
86	- Agent-facing discipline (this `SKILL.md` + `references/remediation.md`).
87	- A single-command project bootstrap (`bootstrap-project.sh`) for repos
88	  without chezmoi or where the user wants the stack in one go.
89	- Session-discovery heuristics (`find-session.sh`) for the "find my
90	  current transcript among many" problem.
91	- An exit-code wrapper (`scan-staged.sh`) agents can branch on before
92	  committing.
93	
94	## Workflow A: commit-time hygiene
95	
96	Default flow when the agent is about to commit feature changes plus
97	chat/plan artifacts.
98	
99	```bash
100	# 1. Make sure the agent knows which session is "ours" — mostly
101	#    relevant when multiple Claude/SpecStory sessions run in the repo.
102	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/find-session.sh
103	
104	# 2. Stage code the usual way, then auto-add agent artifacts.
105	git add path/to/feature/file.ts
106	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh
107	# Use --session-only if you want ONLY the current SpecStory + newest plan;
108	# default stages every dirty *.md in every configured agent dir.
109	
110	# 3. Belt-and-suspenders secret scan before commit. Exit 0 = clean.
111	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/scan-staged.sh || {
112	  # Exit 10/20: leaks found. Jump to references/remediation.md.
113	  echo "Leaks detected — see references/remediation.md before committing." >&2
114	  exit 1
115	}
116	
117	# 4. Commit. pre-commit (installed by bootstrap) runs redact-agent-secrets
118	#    then gitleaks again as a catch-all.
119	git commit -m "feat: ..."
120	```
121	
122	## Workflow B: bootstrap a new project
123	
124	For repos that don't yet have `.pre-commit-config.yaml` / `.gitleaks.toml`
125	installed. Runs once per repo.
126	
127	```bash
128	cd /path/to/new/project
129	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/bootstrap-project.sh \
130	  --install-hook            # optional: auto-stage on every commit
131	
132	# Verify: shake out any existing issues in the working tree.
133	pre-commit run --all-files
134	```
135	
136	What `bootstrap-project.sh` does:
137	
138	1. Drops `.pre-commit-config.yaml` + `.gitleaks.toml` into the repo
139	   (skips if already present unless `--force`). The redactor is a pinned
140	   remote hook (`repo: …/agent-skills`, `rev: ahh-v1.1.0`), **not** a
141	   vendored `scripts/redact_secrets.py` — so `pre-commit autoupdate`
142	   keeps it current everywhere.
143	2. Runs `pre-commit install` (or `uvx pre-commit@4 install` if
144	   pre-commit isn't on `PATH`).
145	3. Audits `.gitignore` / `.git/info/exclude` for patterns that would
146	   silently hide an agent artifact dir — warns without editing.
147	4. Checks `~/.claude/settings.json` for `plansDirectory`; prints the
148	   one-line patch if missing.
149	5. With `--install-hook`: writes a `prepare-commit-msg` hook that calls
150	   `stage-agent-artifacts.sh --session-only --allow-empty` so every
151	   `git commit` auto-attaches the current session file.
152	
153	Migrating a repo off the **old vendored layout** (a committed
154	`scripts/redact_secrets.py` + a `- repo: local` redact hook):
155	
156	```bash
157	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/bootstrap-project.sh --migrate
158	```
159	
160	removes the vendored script and rewrites the local hook into the pinned
161	remote hook, leaving your other hooks and `.gitleaks.toml` untouched
162	(idempotent; safe to re-run).
163	
164	## Workflow C: post-leak remediation
165	
166	When `scan-staged.sh` reports exit `10`/`20`, or the user says "I
167	committed / pushed a secret":
168	
169	1. **STOP** the user from running `git push --force` reflexively.
170	2. Read `references/remediation.md` end-to-end.
171	3. Walk the user through **step 1 (rotate)** regardless of blast
172	   radius. Only after rotation does the question of scrubbing history
173	   become worth discussing.
174	4. Use the decision tree in the runbook to pick the right git action.
175	
176	## Gotchas
177	
178	- **`plansDirectory` project-level sometimes ignored.** Claude Code
179	  issue [#19537](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/19537)
180	  reports project-level `plansDirectory` being ignored in some
181	  versions. After running a `/plan`, verify the file actually landed
182	  where you expected before relying on `stage-agent-artifacts.sh`
183	  picking it up. User-level config (`~/.claude/settings.json` with
184	  `"plansDirectory": "./.claude/plans"`) is the recommended default.
185	- **`gitleaks protect` is deprecated.** Since v8.19.0 use
186	  `gitleaks git --staged --redact` (pre-commit) and
187	  `gitleaks dir <path>` (working directory). The older commands still
188	  work but emit a deprecation notice. This skill uses the modern
189	  syntax everywhere.
190	- **`pre-commit install` is per-clone.** Each teammate must run
191	  `pre-commit install` in their own clone for hooks to fire. CI cannot
192	  be trusted as the single gate — it's second-chance, not last-chance.
193	- **Transcript files can be huge.** A long SpecStory session can exceed
194	  2 MB. The template bumps `check-added-large-files` to `--maxkb=2048`
195	  to avoid false positives, but a very long session can still overflow.
196	  If you hit the limit, rotate sessions (`specstory run claude`
197	  creates a fresh file) instead of raising the cap further.
198	- **Session-UUID divergence between SpecStory CLI and VS Code
199	  extension.** The extension autosaves into `.specstory/history/`
200	  continuously; the CLI (`specstory run claude`) creates one file per
201	  invocation. If both are active you can end up with two transcripts
202	  for what feels like "one session" — mtime-newest wins in
203	  `find-session.sh`.
204	- **Global `core.hooksPath` means bare repos aren't protected.** The
205	  chezmoi setup's global hook runs `.pre-commit-config.yaml` IF it
206	  exists — so a repo without `.pre-commit-config.yaml` has no
207	  protection. Run `bootstrap-project.sh` before the first commit with
208	  agent artifacts, not after.
209	- **Active SpecStory writer can defeat the redact loop.** The standard
210	  `git add → git commit → pre-commit auto-fixes → re-stage → re-commit`
211	  flow assumes the file is **quiescent** during the commit. SpecStory's
212	  `specstory_*_watch` daemon tails the agent transcript continuously,
213	  so if the chat captured `ps -axo args`-style output that contained an
214	  unrelated daemon's secret in argv (e.g. SpecStory's own
215	  `--cloud-token …` flag), every diagnostic command (`grep`, `sed -n
216	  '<line>p'`, `cat | head | tail`) prints the secret again, SpecStory
217	  appends it to the transcript, and the redact-then-restage cycle
218	  never converges. Symptom: pre-commit says "Successfully redacted N
219	  file(s)" but `gitleaks-system` immediately fails on the same line,
220	  re-running `git add && git commit` doesn't help, and `grep -c
221	  '<secret-prefix>' file` shows the count *increasing* over commit
222	  attempts. **Workaround**: a single atomic
223	  `python3 -c "<in-place re.sub>" && git add <file> && git commit -m
224	  "..."` pipeline so the index is frozen before any new specstory write
225	  lands. **Don't** print, grep, or diff the secret line during the
226	  recovery — every print echoes back into the transcript. Diagnose with
227	  `lsof <file>` (looking for `specstory_*` writers) instead. See
228	  `pitfalls/redact-secrets-loop-with-active-specstory-writer.md` in
229	  upstream chezmoi for the full debugging trail.
230	  **Fixed sub-case:** the *bare-phrase* variant of this loop — where the
231	  redactor's own `PRIVATE KEY` substring match kept flagging prose that
232	  merely *discusses* private keys (this skill's docs, or a chat about
233	  redaction) with **no real secret present** — no longer happens.
234	  `redact_secrets.py` now scopes to key *headers* (the
235	  `detect-private-key` BLACKLIST), so prose mentions are ignored and
236	  converge immediately. The atomic-commit workaround above is still
237	  needed for the harder case: a **real** secret an active writer keeps
238	  re-appending. When only the substring redactor (`redact-agent-secrets`)
239	  trips while `gitleaks` + `detect-private-key` pass, it's the false
240	  positive — verify with `gitleaks git --staged` and, if clean, commit
241	  with `SKIP=redact-agent-secrets` (keeps the real gates active).
242	
243	## Available scripts
244	
245	- **`scripts/find-session.sh [--format=specstory|claude|both] [--json]`**
246	  Discover the current agent session files for `$PWD`. TSV default,
247	  `--json` for structured callers. Never exits non-zero (always 0,
248	  empty fields signal absence).
249	
250	- **`scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh [--session-only] [--include-all-plans] [--dry-run] [--allow-empty]`**
251	  `git add` the right agent artifacts before the next commit.
252	  `--session-only` stages only the current SpecStory + newest plan;
253	  default stages every dirty `*.md` in every configured artifact dir.
254	  Refuses to run if there are no code changes (prevents "commit just
255	  transcript"); override with `--allow-empty`.
256	
257	- **`scripts/scan-staged.sh [--redact] [--verbose]`**
258	  Run `gitleaks git --staged` with agent-friendly exit codes
259	  (0 clean / 10 redacted / 20 leaks / 30 gitleaks missing). JSON lines
260	  on stdout, prose diagnostics on stderr.
261	
262	- **`scripts/bootstrap-project.sh [--from-chezmoi] [--install-hook] [--force] [--dry-run]`**
263	  Install `.pre-commit-config.yaml` + `.gitleaks.toml` + the redactor
264	  into the current repo, then run `pre-commit install`. Audits
265	  `.gitignore` and `~/.claude/settings.json` for misconfigurations
266	  (warns, never silently edits).
267	
268	## Bundled assets
269	
270	- `assets/artifact-dirs.txt` — the canonical list of agent artifact
271	  directories (SpecStory, Claude plans, Cursor plans + rules, OpenCode
272	  plans, Spec-kit, Codex). Consumed by `stage-agent-artifacts.sh` and
273	  by `bootstrap-project.sh` when rendering the pre-commit `files:`
274	  regex.

276	  `.pre-commit-config.yaml` with `redact-agent-secrets` + gitleaks +
277	  standard hygiene hooks.
278	- `assets/gitleaks.toml.template` — portable subset of the chezmoi
279	  `.gitleaks.toml` with custom rule IDs + a path-scoped allowlist for

```text
1	# Pre-commit redaction stack
2	
3	The three-layer defense agents can rely on when committing agent
4	transcripts + plan files.
5	
6	```
7	  staged .md (transcript / plan)
8	            │
9	            ▼
10	  Layer 1: redact-agent-secrets   (pre-commit, pinned remote hook)
11	            │  rewrites file in place, re-stages via pre-commit
12	            ▼
13	  Layer 2: gitleaks-system         (pre-commit, github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks)
14	            │  blocks commit if a rule still matches
15	            ▼
16	  Layer 3: scan-staged.sh          (agent-invoked, belt-and-suspenders)
17	            │  run by the agent before `git commit` to branch on exit codes
18	            ▼
19	         git commit
20	```
21	
22	Layers 1 and 2 are installed by `bootstrap-project.sh`. Layer 3 is the
23	wrapper agents are expected to call before committing so they can react
24	to structured exit codes without parsing pre-commit output.
25	
26	## Layer 1: redact-agent-secrets
27	
28	Implemented by `assets/redact_secrets.py` and published as a **pinned
29	remote pre-commit hook** via this repo's root `.pre-commit-hooks.yaml`.
30	Consuming repos reference it in their `.pre-commit-config.yaml`:
31	
32	```yaml
33	- repo: https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills
34	  rev: ahh-v1.1.0
35	  hooks:
36	    - id: redact-agent-secrets
37	```
38	
39	There is no vendored `scripts/redact_secrets.py`, so a fix here reaches
40	every repo via `pre-commit autoupdate` (bumps `rev:`). On each commit:
41	
42	1. Pre-commit matches staged files against the hook's `files:` default
43	   (declared in `.pre-commit-hooks.yaml`, mirroring
44	   `assets/artifact-dirs.txt`). `language: script` runs the file
45	   directly via its `#!/usr/bin/env python3` shebang — stdlib-only, no
46	   env build, no uv/pip.
47	2. `redact_secrets.py --fix` runs gitleaks against those files in staged
48	   mode, gathers findings, and replaces each literal secret with
49	   `first3...last3` (e.g. `sk-proj-abc...xyz`).
50	3. Private-key PEM blocks (`-----BEGIN ... PRIVATE KEY-----` … `-----END
51	   ... PRIVATE KEY-----`) are replaced wholesale with `[REDACTED PEM
52	   PRIVKEY BLOCK]`, and any stray key **header** token (a truncated key,
53	   or a header quoted in prose) with `[REDACTED PRIVKEY HEADER]`. These
54	   headers — *not* the bare phrase `PRIVATE KEY` — are exactly what the
55	   downstream `detect-private-key` hook greps for (its `BLACKLIST`:
56	   `BEGIN … PRIVATE KEY`, `PuTTY-User-Key-File-N`, `BEGIN OpenVPN Static
57	   key V1`), so the redactor scopes to them. Bare `PRIVATE KEY` prose is
58	   left intact on purpose: redacting it mangled legitimate text and,
59	   against a live transcript writer that re-appends the words on every
60	   diagnostic command, never converged (see the redact-loop pitfall in
61	   `SKILL.md`). The two placeholders contain neither a header token nor
62	   the bare phrase, so a second pass is a no-op.
63	4. Any modified file is rewritten on disk. Pre-commit notices and exits
64	   non-zero with "files were modified by this hook" — the user then
65	   `git add`s the redacted files and recommits. Same UX as
66	   trailing-whitespace or end-of-file-fixer.
67	
68	### Why redact (Layer 1) instead of block (Layer 2) for agent artifacts?
69	
70	Because "blocking" a chat transcript on a leak is useless — the secret
71	is already in the file system, in the shell history, in the agent's
72	conversation context. The only defense left is "don't let it hit
73	`origin/`". Rewriting the file is the cheapest way to achieve that
74	while keeping the surrounding prose intact for future readers.
75	
76	## Layer 2: gitleaks-system
77	
78	The upstream `github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks` hook (pinned at `v8.22.1` in
79	the template). Runs after Layer 1 so it sees the redacted file. With
80	`.gitleaks.toml` in the repo root, custom rules apply automatically.
81	
82	### Allowlist design
83	
84	Two allowlists in `gitleaks.toml.template`:
85	
86	- **Global** (`[allowlist]`): tolerates `*_REDACTED*` sentinels emitted
87	  by Layer 1, plus truncated example shapes like `sk-proj-abc...`.
88	- **Path-scoped** (`[[allowlists]]` with `paths`): inside agent
89	  artifact directories, tolerate example markers (`example-key`,
90	  `your-api-key-here`) and truncated example shapes. Both the **path
91	  AND a regex** must match — a real `sk-ant-api03-<95 chars>AA` inside
92	  a transcript still fires.
93	
94	Real leaks take precedence over documentation because gitleaks evaluates
95	the finding's actual bytes, and truncated-example shapes don't have
96	enough entropy to match the strict rules in the first place.
97	
98	## Layer 3: scan-staged.sh
99	
100	Belt-and-suspenders wrapper:
101	
102	```bash
103	bash /path/to/skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/scan-staged.sh
104	```
105	
106	Runs `gitleaks git --staged` and translates the outcome into exit codes
107	agents can branch on:
108	
109	| Exit | Meaning                              | Typical agent reaction                                  |
110	|-----:|--------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------|
111	|    0 | Clean                                | Proceed with `git commit`                               |
112	|   10 | Leaks found, `--redact` passed       | Run `redact_secrets.py --fix`, re-stage, re-run         |
113	|   20 | Leaks found, no redaction            | Rotate secret at provider, then redact + re-stage       |
114	|   30 | gitleaks not installed               | Surface install hint; fall back to bare pre-commit      |
115	|    2 | Not inside a git repo                | Abort or bootstrap a repo first                         |
116	
117	Scripts always emit **JSON-lines findings on stdout** so the agent can
118	feed them to follow-up tooling without parsing prose.
119	
120	## Releasing / updating the pinned hook
121	
122	`assets/redact_secrets.py` is the single source; it's published to
123	consuming repos through this repo's root `.pre-commit-hooks.yaml`, pinned
124	by tag. To ship a fix:
125	
126	```bash
127	# 1. edit assets/redact_secrets.py + tests, run the suite
128	uv run --with pytest pytest skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/tests
129	
130	# 2. tag a new hook release (keep the ahh-v* series for this skill) and push
131	git tag ahh-v1.2.0 && git push origin main --tags
132	
133	# 3. in each consuming repo, bump the rev (or `pre-commit autoupdate`)
134	#    - repo: https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills
135	#      rev: ahh-v1.2.0
136	```
137	
138	**Monorepo caveat:** `pre-commit autoupdate` moves `rev:` to the newest
139	tag on this repo, so an unrelated skill's tag could bump this hook. Keep
140	hook releases on the `ahh-v*` series and, if you need strict isolation,
141	pin a commit SHA in `rev:` instead of a tag.
142	
143	**Migrating an old vendored repo** (committed `scripts/redact_secrets.py`
144	+ a `- repo: local` redact hook) to the pinned hook:
145	
146	```bash
147	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/bootstrap-project.sh --migrate
148	```
149	
150	`DEFAULT_PATHS` in the script and the `files:` default in
151	`.pre-commit-hooks.yaml` both mirror `assets/artifact-dirs.txt` — keep
152	the three in sync when adding an artifact directory.
153	
154	## Inline allowlist pragmas
155	
156	For one-off false positives that don't deserve a config change, gitleaks
157	accepts inline `#gitleaks:allow` on the same line as the match. Use
158	sparingly — every pragma is an opportunity for a real secret to ride
159	along in review.
160	
161	```
162	# Example call pattern:
163	# curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-proj-fake1234..." #gitleaks:allow
164	```
165	
166	For whole-file exceptions, prefer adding a path to `.gitleaksignore`
167	(one glob per line, gitignore syntax).
168	
169	## Cross-reference
170	
171	- [`transcript-session-discovery.md`](./transcript-session-discovery.md)
172	  — how we locate which files to scan.
173	- [`remediation.md`](./remediation.md) — what to do when Layer 3 fires
174	  on an already-pushed commit.
175	- [`../assets/artifact-dirs.txt`](../assets/artifact-dirs.txt) — the
176	  shared source of truth for "which directories contain agent artifacts".
177
```

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# new-skill.sh — Scaffold a new agent skill in the npx-skills-compatible layout.
3	#
4	# Three placement scopes (auto-detected by default, override with --local /
5	# --project / --global):
6	#
7	#   LOCAL    Publishing-repo workflow (this very repo). Canonical content lives
8	#            under <repo>/skills/local/<name>/ (or skills/vendor/<name>/ with
9	#            --vendor), and discovery symlinks are added at
10	#            <repo>/.agents/skills/<name> and <repo>/.claude/skills/<name>
11	#            -> ../../skills/{local,vendor}/<name>.
12	#
13	#   PROJECT  Generic per-project install. Canonical content at
14	#            <repo>/.agents/skills/<name>/ (universal agents like Cursor /
15	#            Codex / OpenCode / Warp pick this up directly), plus a relative
16	#            symlink at <repo>/.claude/skills/<name> -> ../../.agents/skills/<name>
17	#            (and other already-present non-universal agent dirs).
18	#
19	#   GLOBAL   System-wide install. Canonical content at ~/.agents/skills/<name>/
20	#            plus a relative symlink at ~/.claude/skills/<name> ->
21	#            ../../.agents/skills/<name> (and any other detected agent dir).
22	#
23	# Auto-detection precedence (when no scope flag given):
24	#   1. publishing repo (vendor.yaml, skills/local/, or
25	#      skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json found walking up) -> LOCAL
26	#   2. inside a git repo (.git found walking up)                 -> PROJECT
27	#   3. otherwise                                                 -> GLOBAL
28	#
29	# Bash 3.2 compatible (works on stock macOS — no mapfile, no ${var,,},
30	# no [[ -v var ]]).
31	
32	set -euo pipefail
33	
34	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
35	SKILL_DIR="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
36	ASSETS_DIR="$SKILL_DIR/assets"
37	
38	usage() {
39	  cat <<'EOF'
40	Usage: new-skill.sh [OPTIONS] <skill-name>
41	
42	Scaffold a new agent skill with the standard layout (SKILL.md, references/,
43	scripts/, assets/) seeded from skill-author's templates, then place it where
44	the active scope says it belongs and add discovery symlinks for non-universal
45	agents.
46	
47	Scope (mutually exclusive — auto-detected if omitted):
48	  --local            Force LOCAL mode (this publishing repo's skills/local/).
49	                     Requires a vendor.yaml / skills/local/ / skills/.claude-plugin
50	                     anchor walking up from --root or CWD.
51	  --project          Force PROJECT mode (<repo>/.agents/skills/<name>/).
52	                     Requires a git repo root (.git) walking up.
53	  --global           Force GLOBAL mode (~/.agents/skills/<name>/).
54	
55	Other options:
56	  --vendor           In LOCAL mode, place under skills/vendor/<name>/ instead of
57	                     skills/local/. (Rare — vendored skills normally come via
58	                     vendor.yaml + scripts/sync-vendor.sh.)
59	  --root DIR         Override repo / project root discovery.
60	  --no-symlinks      Skip the agent-dir discovery symlinks (just write the
61	                     canonical dir). Useful for CI / packaging tests.
62	  --dry-run          Print what would be created without writing.
63	  --force            Overwrite if the target canonical directory already exists.
64	                     Existing symlinks are always replaced.
65	  --help, -h         Show this help and exit.
66	
67	Examples:
68	  bash new-skill.sh my-skill                # auto-detect scope
69	  bash new-skill.sh --project my-skill      # force project (.agents/skills)
70	  bash new-skill.sh --global my-skill       # force user-wide (~/.agents/skills)
71	  bash new-skill.sh --local my-skill        # force skills/local/ (publish repo)
72	  bash new-skill.sh --dry-run my-skill      # see what would happen
73	  bash new-skill.sh --root /path/to/repo my-skill
74	
75	Output:
76	  Single JSON object on stdout (parseable by an agent), prose on stderr.
77	  Keys: skill, mode, canonical, symlinks[], next_steps[].
78	
79	Exit codes:
80	  0  success
81	  1  invalid arguments
82	  2  target canonical directory already exists (use --force to overwrite)
83	  3  scope precondition failed (e.g. --local outside a publishing repo,
84	     --project outside a git repo, template missing)
85	  4  symlink creation produced a broken link (post-write verification failed)
86	EOF
87	}
88	
89	log()  { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
90	die()  { printf 'error: %s\n' "$1" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }
91	
92	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
93	# Arg parsing
94	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
95	NAME=""
96	ROOT_OVERRIDE=""
97	DRY_RUN=0
98	FORCE=0
99	VENDOR=0
100	NO_SYMLINKS=0
101	MODE=""  # "", "local", "project", "global"
102	
103	set_mode() {
104	  if [ -n "$MODE" ] && [ "$MODE" != "$1" ]; then
105	    die "conflicting scope flags: already set to --$MODE, got --$1" 1
106	  fi
107	  MODE="$1"
108	}

110	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
111	  case "$1" in
112	    --local)        set_mode local;   shift ;;
113	    --project)      set_mode project; shift ;;
114	    --global)       set_mode global;  shift ;;
115	    --vendor)       VENDOR=1; shift ;;
116	    --root)         ROOT_OVERRIDE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
117	    --no-symlinks)  NO_SYMLINKS=1; shift ;;
