147	# Walk up from $1 looking for a directory matching the predicate (a callable
148	# that takes the candidate dir and returns 0 if it matches).
149	walk_up_for() {
150	  local start="$1" predicate="$2"
151	  local cur="$start"
152	  while [ "$cur" != "/" ] && [ -n "$cur" ]; do
153	    if "$predicate" "$cur"; then
154	      printf '%s\n' "$cur"
155	      return 0
156	    fi
157	    cur="$(dirname "$cur")"
158	  done

179	GIT_ROOT=""

196	SUBDIR_LABEL=""

302	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
303	# Helpers
304	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
305	
306	create_dir() {
307	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
308	    log "[dry-run] mkdir -p $1"
309	  else
310	    mkdir -p "$1"
311	  fi
312	}
313	
314	write_template() {
315	  local src="$1" dst="$2"
316	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
317	    log "[dry-run] cp $src -> $dst"
318	    return 0
319	  fi
320	  if [ ! -f "$src" ]; then
321	    die "template missing: $src" 3
322	  fi
323	  cp "$src" "$dst"
324	}
325	
326	substitute() {
327	  local file="$1"
328	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
329	    log "[dry-run] would substitute placeholders in $file"
330	    return 0
331	  fi
332	  # Bash 3.2 safe: sed -i with a backup, then drop the backup file (the BSD
333	  # vs GNU sed split is the reason we go through a .bak detour).
334	  sed -i.bak \
335	    -e "s/SKILL_NAME_PLACEHOLDER/$NAME/g" \
336	    -e "s/SKILL_TITLE_PLACEHOLDER/$(printf '%s' "$NAME" | tr '-' ' ')/g" \
337	    "$file"
338	  rm -f "${file}.bak"
339	}
340	
341	# Symlink at <linkdir>/<NAME> -> ../../<rel-target>, then verify the link is
342	# resolvable (test -e). All three placement scopes use the same fixed two-
343	# levels-up form because both <linkdir> and <canonical-parent> are exactly
344	# two levels under the base dir (.claude/skills/, .agents/skills/, etc.) —
345	# see pitfalls/symlink-target-relative-to-symlink-not-cwd.md.
346	#
347	# Args: <link-skills-dir> <relative-target-suffix>
348	# Example: link_into "$BASE_DIR/.claude/skills" "skills/local"
349	#          -> creates .claude/skills/<NAME> -> ../../skills/local/<NAME>
350	link_into() {
351	  local link_skills_dir="$1" target_suffix="$2"
352	  local link_path="$link_skills_dir/$NAME"
353	  local relative_target="../../$target_suffix/$NAME"
354	
355	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
356	    log "[dry-run] mkdir -p $link_skills_dir && ln -snf $relative_target $link_path"
357	    SYMLINKS_CREATED="$SYMLINKS_CREATED
358	$link_path -> $relative_target"
359	    return 0
360	  fi
361	
362	  mkdir -p "$link_skills_dir"
363	
364	  # Replace any existing entry (symlink, broken symlink, dir, or file). We do
365	  # NOT recursively delete real content here on purpose — if the path is a
366	  # real directory, the user pointed --force at the wrong place.
367	  if [ -L "$link_path" ]; then
368	    rm -f "$link_path"
369	  elif [ -e "$link_path" ]; then
370	    if [ "$FORCE" = "1" ]; then
371	      rm -rf "$link_path"
372	    else
373	      die "would clobber non-symlink at $link_path (use --force to replace)" 2
374	    fi
375	  fi
376	
377	  ln -s "$relative_target" "$link_path"
378	
379	  if [ ! -e "$link_path/SKILL.md" ]; then
380	    die "created symlink is dangling: $link_path -> $relative_target (resolved from $link_skills_dir). This is the pitfall described in pitfalls/symlink-target-relative-to-symlink-not-cwd.md." 4
381	  fi
382	
383	  SYMLINKS_CREATED="$SYMLINKS_CREATED
384	$link_path -> $relative_target"
385	}
386	
387	# Resolve the target suffix that all symlinks for the current mode share.
388	# - LOCAL:   skills/local  (or skills/vendor with --vendor)
389	# - PROJECT: .agents/skills
390	# - GLOBAL:  .agents/skills
391	target_suffix_for_mode() {
392	  case "$MODE" in
393	    local)   [ "$VENDOR" = "1" ] && printf 'skills/vendor\n' || printf 'skills/local\n' ;;
394	    project) printf '.agents/skills\n' ;;
395	    global)  printf '.agents/skills\n' ;;
396	  esac
397	}
398	
399	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
400	# Scaffold the canonical directory
401	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
402	log "Mode:      $MODE"
403	log "Base:      $BASE_DIR"
404	log "Canonical: $CANONICAL_DIR"
405	
406	create_dir "$CANONICAL_DIR"
407	create_dir "$CANONICAL_DIR/references"
408	create_dir "$CANONICAL_DIR/scripts"
409	create_dir "$CANONICAL_DIR/assets"
410	
411	write_template "$ASSETS_DIR/SKILL.md.template" "$CANONICAL_DIR/SKILL.md"
412	substitute "$CANONICAL_DIR/SKILL.md"
413	
414	# .gitkeep so empty subdirs survive `git add`.
415	if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "0" ]; then
416	  for sub in references scripts assets; do
417	    if [ -z "$(ls -A "$CANONICAL_DIR/$sub" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
418	      : > "$CANONICAL_DIR/$sub/.gitkeep"
419	    fi
420	  done
421	fi
422	
423	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
424	# Fan-out symlinks
425	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
426	SYMLINKS_CREATED=""
427	TARGET_SUFFIX="$(target_suffix_for_mode)"
428	
429	if [ "$NO_SYMLINKS" = "1" ]; then
430	  log "Symlinks:  skipped (--no-symlinks)"
431	else
432	  if [ "$MODE" = "local" ]; then
433	    # In LOCAL mode also add the .agents/skills convenience link in addition to
434	    # .claude/skills, because this repo dogfoods .agents/skills as a discovery
435	    # farm even though it isn't a "consumer install".
436	    link_into "$BASE_DIR/.agents/skills" "$TARGET_SUFFIX"
437	  fi
438	
439	  # claude-code: always fanned out (most-used non-universal agent).
440	  link_into "$BASE_DIR/.claude/skills" "$TARGET_SUFFIX"
441	
442	  # Other non-universal agents: only if their config root already exists at
443	  # $BASE_DIR (mirrors upstream's "don't create .windsurf/ unless present"
444	  # rule). Use a heredoc rather than a pipe so the while-loop runs in the
445	  # parent shell — preserves SYMLINKS_CREATED mutations and lets `die` exit
446	  # the script.
447	  while IFS='|' read -r root_dir sub; do
448	    [ -n "$root_dir" ] || continue
449	    case "$root_dir" in \#*) continue ;; esac
450	    if [ -d "$BASE_DIR/$root_dir" ]; then
451	      link_into "$BASE_DIR/$root_dir/$sub" "$TARGET_SUFFIX"
452	    fi
453	  done <<EOF
454	$NONUNIVERSAL_AGENTS_IF_PRESENT
455	EOF
456	fi
457	
458	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
459	# Structured success output
460	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
461	if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
462	  log "Dry run complete. Re-run without --dry-run to actually create files."
463	  exit 0
464	fi
465	
466	# Build a JSON array of symlinks for the structured output. bash 3.2 safe.
467	json_symlinks() {
468	  printf '['
469	  local first=1 line
470	  # Read from a temp string; the while-loop body runs in the parent shell
471	  # because we use here-string, so we can mutate `first`.
472	  while IFS= read -r line; do
473	    [ -n "$line" ] || continue
474	    if [ "$first" = "1" ]; then first=0; else printf ','; fi
475	    # line is "<link> -> <target>" — keep that as a single string.
476	    printf '"%s"' "$(printf '%s' "$line" | sed 's/"/\\"/g')"
477	  done <<EOF
478	$SYMLINKS_CREATED
479	EOF
480	  printf ']'
481	}
482	
483	NEXT_STEPS="\"Edit $CANONICAL_DIR/SKILL.md to fill in description and workflow\",\"Run lint-skill.sh $CANONICAL_DIR to verify\""
484	
485	printf '{"skill":"%s","mode":"%s","canonical":"%s","symlinks":%s,"next_steps":[%s]}\n' \
486	  "$NAME" "$MODE" "$CANONICAL_DIR" "$(json_symlinks)" "$NEXT_STEPS"
487

102	## SKILL.md Format

110	context (Cursor and Claude Code load whatever resolves under those dirs).
111	They are unrelated to distribution — downstream users get skills via
112	`npx skills add ...` + `marketplace.json` regardless of these links.
113	
114	`scripts/new-skill.sh --local` (run by the `skill-author` skill) creates
115	both links automatically. **Only keep them for skills that are genuinely
116	useful while working _on this repo_** — e.g. `skill-author`,
117	`mkdocs-site-bootstrap`. Skills authored here purely for downstream use
118	(e.g. `fastapi-ai-*`, `dvc-ml-workflow`, `mlflow-tracking`) should **not**
119	be symlinked: they would load into every in-repo agent session and just
120	bloat/pollute context without ever being exercised here. The canonical copy
121	under `skills/local/<name>/` is all that's needed for distribution.
122	
123	To author a downstream-only skill without the links, either:

125	```bash

127	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh --local --no-symlinks <name>

2	# scan-staged.sh — run gitleaks on the current staged diff with

4	#
5	# Bash 3.2 compatible (stock macOS).
6	
7	set -euo pipefail
8	
9	usage() {
10	  cat <<'EOF'
11	Usage: scan-staged.sh [OPTIONS]
12	
13	Scan the staged diff for secrets using `gitleaks git --staged`. Intended
14	as the "last line of defense" wrapper agents call before `git commit` so
15	they can branch on structured exit codes.
16	
17	Options:
18	  --redact           Pass --redact to gitleaks (default: off; findings
19	                     print the literal secret for debugging).
20	  --no-redact        Explicit opt-out of --redact (overrides --redact).
21	  --config PATH      Path to .gitleaks.toml (default: repo root if present).
22	  --verbose          Print gitleaks' own output to stderr.
23	  --help, -h         Show this help and exit.
24	
25	Output (stdout):
26	  - If clean: no output.
27	  - If leaks found: one JSON object per line with the finding details.
28	
29	Exit codes:
30	  0   clean — no secrets found
31	  10  leaks found (and redacted if --redact was passed)
32	  20  leaks found, not redacted (caller must rotate + re-stage)
33	  30  gitleaks binary not installed
34	  40  gitleaks error (bad config, unreadable repo, etc.)
35	  1   invalid arguments
36	  2   not inside a git repo
37	EOF
38	}
39	
40	log()  { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
41	die()  { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }
42	
43	REDACT=0
44	CONFIG=""
45	VERBOSE=0
46	
47	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
48	  case "$1" in
49	    --redact)     REDACT=1; shift ;;
50	    --no-redact)  REDACT=0; shift ;;
51	    --config)     CONFIG="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
52	    --config=*)   CONFIG="${1#--config=}"; shift ;;
53	    --verbose)    VERBOSE=1; shift ;;
54	    --help|-h)    usage; exit 0 ;;
55	    -*)           die "unknown flag: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
56	    *)            die "unexpected positional arg: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
57	  esac
58	done
59	
60	# Check prerequisites.
61	if ! command -v gitleaks >/dev/null 2>&1; then
62	  log "gitleaks not installed. Install hints:"
63	  log "  macOS:   brew install gitleaks"
64	  log "  Linux:   https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/releases"
65	  exit 30
66	fi
67	
68	if ! git rev-parse --show-toplevel >/dev/null 2>&1; then
69	  die "not inside a git repo" 2
70	fi
71	cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
72	
73	# Auto-discover config if not specified.
74	if [ -z "$CONFIG" ] && [ -f ".gitleaks.toml" ]; then
75	  CONFIG=".gitleaks.toml"
76	fi

78	report_path="$(mktemp -t gitleaks-report.XXXXXX.json)"
79	trap 'rm -f "$report_path"' EXIT
80	
81	# Assemble the command. Post v8.19.0 `gitleaks git --staged` replaces the
82	# deprecated `gitleaks protect --staged`.
83	cmd=(gitleaks git --staged
84	     --report-format json
85	     --report-path "$report_path"
86	     --exit-code 0)
87	[ -n "$CONFIG" ] && cmd+=(--config "$CONFIG")
88	[ "$REDACT" = "1" ] && cmd+=(--redact)
89	
90	# Capture gitleaks' own exit code — with `--exit-code 0` it returns 0
91	# whether leaks are found or not, so a non-zero exit means the tool itself
92	# failed (config error, unreadable repo, etc.).
93	stderr_capture="$(mktemp -t gitleaks-stderr.XXXXXX)"
94	trap 'rm -f "$report_path" "$stderr_capture"' EXIT
95	
96	gl_rc=0
97	if [ "$VERBOSE" = "1" ]; then
98	  "${cmd[@]}" >&2 2>>"$stderr_capture" || gl_rc=$?
99	else
100	  "${cmd[@]}" >/dev/null 2>"$stderr_capture" || gl_rc=$?
101	fi
102	
103	if [ "$gl_rc" -ne 0 ]; then
104	  log "gitleaks failed to run (exit $gl_rc). Tail of its stderr:"
105	  tail -n 20 "$stderr_capture" >&2 || true
106	  exit 40
107	fi
108	
109	# Gitleaks writes an empty file when truly clean, or `[]` when the report
110	# format is JSON and there are zero findings. Normalize both to "clean".
111	if [ ! -s "$report_path" ]; then
112	  exit 0
113	fi
114	
115	finding_count=0
116	if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
117	  finding_count=$(python3 - "$report_path" <<'PY'

121	        data = json.load(f)
122	except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError):
123	    print(0)

126	PY
127	)
128	else

130	  case "$(tr -d '[:space:]' < "$report_path")" in
131	    ""|"[]") finding_count=0 ;;
132	    *)        finding_count=1 ;;

135	
136	if [ "$finding_count" -eq 0 ]; then

141	# agent consumption. Findings file is a JSON *array*; slice it into lines
142	# using python3 — avoid adding a jq dependency.
143	if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
144	  python3 - "$report_path" <<'PY'
145	import json, sys
146	with open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8") as f:
147	    data = json.load(f)
148	for finding in data:
149	    # Keep only the most useful fields; caller can re-open the raw report.
150	    slim = {
151	        "rule_id": finding.get("RuleID"),
152	        "file": finding.get("File"),
153	        "line": finding.get("StartLine"),
154	        "commit": finding.get("Commit") or "STAGED",
155	        "match": finding.get("Match"),
156	    }
157	    print(json.dumps(slim, ensure_ascii=False))
158	PY
159	else

161	  cat "$report_path"
162	fi

1	---
2	name: project-knowledge-harness
3	description: Set up a structured project memory for any software project — TODO.md as priority/effort-tagged index of future work, backlog/ for resume-friendly research/design notes on P? items, and pitfalls/ as a symptom-grep-able knowledge base of past traps. Use when a user wants somewhere to record "maybe later" ideas, freeze troubleshooting state, capture trade-off analysis, or stop re-debugging the same problem.
4	---
5	
6	# project-knowledge-harness
7	
8	A lightweight, file-based memory harness for any software project.
9	
10	Three surfaces, sharply separated by **time direction** and **access pattern**:
11	
12	| Surface | Time | Question it answers | Access pattern |
13	|---|---|---|---|
14	| `TODO.md` | Future | "What might we do later?" | Read top to bottom (priority lanes) |
15	| `backlog/<slug>.md` | Future | "What was the analysis behind this idea?" | Indexed from `TODO.md` |
16	| `pitfalls/<slug>.md` | **Past** | **"I see error X — has this happened before?"** | **Grep symptom keywords** |
17	
18	Plus, in projects that already have agent contracts, `AGENTS.md` Hard
19	invariants answer "What rules MUST agents follow?". Pitfalls *graduate* to
20	Hard invariants when serious enough — see
21	[`references/when-to-add-docs.md`](references/when-to-add-docs.md).
22	
23	## When to use this skill
24	
25	Use this skill when the user surfaces any of:
26	
27	- A long-term TODO list with no home, or a messy `TODO.md` that needs
28	  structure (signals: "where should ideas go?", "maybe later", "工程量太大需要再評估")
29	- A debugging session worth saving (signals: "keep solving the same problem
30	  twice", "save this troubleshooting", "踩過的坑", "TROUBLESHOOTING.md
31	  scattered across docs/")
32	- A request to consolidate `IDEAS.md` / `ROADMAP.md` / `WISHLIST.md` /
33	  `LESSONS.md` files
34	
35	Do NOT use this skill for active sprint planning (use issue trackers),
36	ephemeral agent scratchpads (use `.claude/plans/`), or current feature
37	documentation (use `docs/`).
38	
39	## How to apply this skill (default workflow)
40	
41	The skill bundles five scripts and several templates. **Default to the
42	init script** for setup, and **default to `add-todo.sh` / `sweep-inbox.sh`
43	for capture** rather than asking the agent to edit `TODO.md` by hand.
44	
45	```
46	scripts/
47	  init.sh         # one-shot setup of TODO.md + backlog/ + pitfalls/
48	                  # + agent guidance + README snippet
49	  todo-kanban.sh  # validate TODO.md format and render kanban-style board
50	  add-todo.sh     # insert a structured entry into the right ## P* lane
51	  promote-todo.sh # move an active TODO item to ## Done with the right syntax
52	  sweep-inbox.sh  # triage backlog/inbox.md into TODO.md via add-todo.sh
53	```
54	
55	### 1. Run `scripts/init.sh` against the target repo
56	
57	```sh
58	scripts/init.sh \
59	  --target /path/to/project \
60	  --project-name "My Project" \
61	  --deployment chezmoi   # or npm | pip | docker | none
62	```
63	
64	The script:
65	
66	1. Creates `TODO.md`, `backlog/README.md`, `pitfalls/README.md` from
67	   `assets/*.template`, substituting placeholders.
68	2. Appends an agent-guidance snippet to `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` (auto-detected,
69	   override with `--agent-contract`).
70	3. Appends a "Roadmap & lessons learned" section to `README.md`.
71	4. Runs `scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only TODO.md` so any drift is
72	   caught immediately.
73	5. Prints the deployment-exclusion lines you should add manually (it does
74	   not edit ignore files — see
75	   [`references/deployment-exclusion.md`](references/deployment-exclusion.md)).
76	
77	`init.sh` is idempotent: existing files are skipped unless `--force` is
78	given, and snippets append only if a sentinel marker is missing.
79	
80	### 2. Mid-conversation, when the user surfaces a "maybe later" idea
81	
82	Signals: "maybe later", "nice to have", "if I'm interested",
83	"工程量太大需要再評估", "先記下來", "not now but…".
84	
85	1. If `TODO.md` doesn't exist yet, run `scripts/init.sh` first.
86	2. **Default path — call `scripts/add-todo.sh`** with the priority,
87	   effort, title, and description. This inserts the canonical line into
88	   the right `## P*` lane and re-validates. Add `--backlog` if the
89	   conversation produced enough investigation that a `backlog/<slug>.md`
90	   doc is worth scaffolding.
91	
92	   ```sh
93	   scripts/add-todo.sh --priority "P?" --effort M \
94	     --title "Try Rspress for docs" \
95	     --description "Evaluate AI-native docs framework alternative"
96	   ```
97	
98	3. **Quick-capture path — append to `backlog/inbox.md`** when the user
99	   isn't sure of priority/effort yet, or is mid-thought:
100	
101	   ```sh
102	   echo "- $UNSTRUCTURED_THOUGHT" >> backlog/inbox.md
103	   ```
104	
105	   Later (this session or next), run `scripts/sweep-inbox.sh` to
106	   formalize the loose lines into `TODO.md` one at a time. The sweeper
107	   prompts for missing fields per line; in `--batch` mode it only
108	   processes lines that already have `priority=… effort=… title="…"
109	   description="…"` pairs and leaves ambiguous ones in place.
110	
111	4. **Manual edit path — only when scripts can't help.** Use the syntax
112	   from [`references/tag-schema.md`](references/tag-schema.md) and run
113	   `scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only` afterwards.
114	
115	5. If you wrote a `backlog/<slug>.md` (either via `--backlog` or by
116	   hand), make sure the TODO line ends with
117	   ` → [research](backlog/<slug>.md)` so the index points to the doc.
118	
119	### 3. Mid-conversation, when you finish debugging something tricky
120	
121	Signals: "phew, that took a while", "weird, the error didn't say anything
122	about X", "this is the third time we've hit this", or you find yourself
123	reconstructing context that isn't in any doc.
124	
125	1. Create `pitfalls/<symptom-slug>.md` immediately from
126	   `assets/pitfall-doc.md.template`, while the trace is fresh. Title the
127	   doc by the **symptom**, not the root cause — you'll search by what
128	   you're seeing, not by what you eventually learned.
129	2. Copy verbatim error messages — never paraphrase, it kills grep-ability.
130	3. If the trap is severe (silent corruption / cross-machine recurrence /
131	   non-obvious workaround), surface it: "should this graduate to a Hard
132	   invariant in AGENTS.md?" — see
133	   [`references/when-to-add-docs.md`](references/when-to-add-docs.md).
134	
135	### 4. When implementing a `TODO.md` item
136	
137	In the same commit:
138	
139	1. Run `scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<what shipped>"`.
140	   It removes the active line and inserts the dated `Done` entry, then
141	   re-validates. It refuses to run if the substring matches zero or more
142	   than one active item.
143	2. If a `backlog/<slug>.md` exists, set its `Status: shipped` (don't
144	   delete — historical record may inform adjacent decisions).
145	3. If shipping uncovered a trap, write a `pitfalls/<slug>.md` for it.
146	
147	## When a TODO entry needs a `backlog/` doc, when a debug needs a `pitfalls/` doc
148	
149	Decision rules and the upgrade path to `AGENTS.md` invariants live in
150	[`references/when-to-add-docs.md`](references/when-to-add-docs.md). Read it
151	the first time you set up the harness; consult it again whenever you're
152	unsure which surface a piece of knowledge belongs in.
153	
154	## Tag schema
155	
156	Two orthogonal axes, validated by `scripts/todo-kanban.sh`. See
157	[`references/tag-schema.md`](references/tag-schema.md) for the full schema,
158	useful tag combinations, and the exact validator-checked syntax.
159	
160	## Anti-patterns
161	
162	Common mistakes to avoid (e.g., spawning `IDEAS.md` alongside `TODO.md`,
163	titling pitfalls by root cause, paraphrasing errors). Full list in
164	[`references/anti-patterns.md`](references/anti-patterns.md).
165	
166	## Deployment exclusion
167	
168	`TODO.md`, `backlog/`, and `pitfalls/` are maintainer-facing repo metadata,
169	not files to ship. Cheatsheet for chezmoi / npm / pip / Docker in
170	[`references/deployment-exclusion.md`](references/deployment-exclusion.md).
171	`scripts/init.sh --deployment ...` prints the exact lines to add.
172	
173	## Templates and bundled assets
174	
175	- `assets/TODO.md.template` — `TODO.md` skeleton with example items per lane
176	- `assets/backlog-README.md.template` — `backlog/` index + when-to-add rules
177	- `assets/backlog-doc.md.template` — single backlog doc (context-first)
178	- `assets/pitfalls-README.md.template` — `pitfalls/` index + cross-reference
179	  table for traps documented elsewhere
180	- `assets/pitfall-doc.md.template` — single pitfall doc (symptom-first)
181	- `assets/agent-guidance.md.template` — snippet for `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md`
182	- `assets/readme-roadmap.md.template` — snippet for project `README.md`
183	- `scripts/init.sh` — one-shot setup
184	- `scripts/todo-kanban.sh` — validator + Markdown kanban renderer
185	  (also supports `--json` and `--validate-only`)
186	- `scripts/add-todo.sh` — structured insert into `## P*` lane;
187	  `--backlog` also scaffolds `backlog/<slug>.md`
188	- `scripts/promote-todo.sh` — atomic active-→-Done move with re-validation
189	- `scripts/sweep-inbox.sh` — triage `backlog/inbox.md` → `add-todo.sh`
190	
191	## Reference implementation
192	
193	A live example of this harness is at
194	[`daviddwlee84/dotfiles`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles):
195	
196	- `TODO.md`, `backlog/`, `pitfalls/` directories at repo root
197	- `AGENTS.md` `### Long-term backlog → TODO.md + backlog/` and
198	  `### Past pitfalls → pitfalls/` sections
199	- `README.md` `## Roadmap & lessons learned` section
200
```

1	# Pre-commit hook manifest for the agent-history-hygiene skill.
2	# https://pre-commit.com/#creating-new-hooks
3	#
4	# Consume from any repo's .pre-commit-config.yaml:
5	#
6	#   - repo: https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills
7	#     rev: ahh-v1.1.0            # bump with `pre-commit autoupdate`
8	#     hooks:
9	#       - id: redact-agent-secrets
10	#
11	# `pre-commit autoupdate` tracks the newest tag on this repo. Because this is a
12	# multi-skill monorepo, keep this hook's releases on the `ahh-v*` tag series
13	# (or pin a commit SHA in `rev:`) so an unrelated skill's tag can't silently
14	# bump this hook.
15	#
16	# language: script -> pre-commit runs the file directly (its `#!/usr/bin/env
17	# python3` shebang picks the interpreter); the redactor is stdlib-only, so no
18	# env is built and no uv/pip install is needed. It scans staged files itself
19	# (pass_filenames: false) and rewrites any leak in place, so pre-commit reports
20	# "files were modified by this hook" and you re-stage + recommit.
21	- id: redact-agent-secrets
22	  name: Auto-redact secrets in agent artifacts
23	  description: >-
24	    Redact leaked secrets in agent transcript/plan artifacts (SpecStory,
25	    Claude/Cursor/OpenCode plans, spec-kit, Codex) before they are committed.
26	  entry: skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/assets/redact_secrets.py --fix
27	  language: script
28	  pass_filenames: false

1	---
2	name: slurm-hpc
3	description: Generic Slurm/HPC know-how for any cluster. Use when the user writes or debugs sbatch/srun batch scripts, requests resources (--mem/--cpus-per-task/--gres/--time/partitions), reads job state with squeue/sacct/sinfo/scontrol, cancels jobs, or reasons about resource isolation — cgroup CPU/RAM limits and GPU GRES (gpu vs shard vs mps vs MIG) and which of them actually fence VRAM so a misbehaving job fails alone.
4	---
5	
6	# slurm-hpc — generic Slurm workload-manager know-how
7	
8	Portable Slurm reference for authoring batch jobs and reasoning about resource
9	isolation on any cluster. Not tied to a specific site — for a specific repo's
10	recipes and layout, prefer that project's own skill.
11	
12	## When to use
13	
14	- Writing or fixing an `sbatch` script, or an `srun` command line.
15	- Choosing resource requests (CPUs, memory, GPUs, time, partition).
16	- Reading job/queue/node state (`squeue`, `sacct`, `sinfo`, `scontrol`).
17	- Reasoning about what isolates jobs (cgroups) and what fences GPU VRAM.
18	
19	## When NOT to use
20	
21	- Operating a specific project's cluster with its own recipes → use that repo's skill.
22	- Designing cluster provisioning/config from scratch → that's admin work, not this.
23	
24	## Batch script skeleton
25	
26	```bash
27	#!/bin/bash
28	#SBATCH --job-name=train
29	#SBATCH --partition=<partition>       # see `sinfo`
30	#SBATCH --gres=gpu:1                  # GPUs (see GPU section)
31	#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=8
32	#SBATCH --mem=32G                     # per-node; enforced as a hard cgroup cap
33	#SBATCH --time=02:00:00               # job killed at this wall-clock limit
34	#SBATCH --output=logs/%x_%j.out       # %x=name %j=jobid
35	srun python train.py
36	```
37	
38	Submit `sbatch script.sh`; inspect `squeue -j <id>`; after it ends,
39	`sacct -j <id> --format=JobID,State,ExitCode,Elapsed,MaxRSS,ReqTRES,AllocTRES`.
40	Cancel `scancel <id>`. `--start` on squeue estimates a pending job's start.
41	
42	## Resource requests
43	
44	- `--mem=<N>G` / `--mem-per-cpu=<N>G` — real memory; with cgroups this is a
45	  **hard cap** (see below). `--cpus-per-task` + `--ntasks` set core count.
46	- `--gres=gpu:N` or `--gres=gpu:<type>:N` (e.g. `gpu:a100:2`).
47	- `--time` is mandatory discipline on most clusters; jobs are killed at it.
48	- `--exclusive` gives the whole node. Partitions (`sinfo`) gate limits/priority.
49	
50	## Isolation: what actually fences a misbehaving job
51	
52	**CPU/RAM (cgroups, if the site enables `task/cgroup` + `ConstrainCores/RAMSpace`):**
53	a job is pinned to its cores (cpuset) and hard-capped at `--mem`. Exceeding
54	`--mem` triggers the **kernel cgroup OOM killer inside that job's cgroup only**
55	— the job dies alone; neighbours and the host are untouched. A thread-bomb
56	only saturates its own cores. This is real isolation and is the norm.
57	
58	**GPU VRAM — the gap.** Allocating a GPU does NOT cap its memory:
59	
60	| Method | VRAM isolation | Misbehaving job fails alone? |
61	|---|---|---|
62	| `--gres=gpu:N` (whole card) | n/a (owns it) | — |
63	| `--gres=shard:N` | **none** — accounting only | ❌ can OOM the whole card |
64	| `--gres=mps:N` (plain) | none | ❌ |
65	| `--gres=mps:N` + `CUDA_MPS_PINNED_DEVICE_MEM_LIMIT` | enforced cap | ✅ OOMs at its cap |
66	| **MIG** (`--gres=gpu:1g.5gb:1`) | **hardware slice** | ✅ strongest |
67	
68	Read `references/gpu-isolation.md` when the task is specifically about capping
69	or partitioning GPU VRAM, or choosing between shard/mps/MIG.
70	
71	## Reference files
72	
73	- `references/gpu-isolation.md` — read when capping/partitioning GPU VRAM or
74	  choosing shard vs mps vs MIG; has the config snippets and enforcement details.
75	
76	## Gotchas
77	
78	- **`--gres=shard:N` and plain `--gres=mps:N` do NOT fence VRAM.** Sharing a
79	  GPU ≠ isolating it. Only MPS *with a pinned memory limit set*, or MIG,
80	  enforces a per-job VRAM ceiling. A job with a wrong batch size otherwise OOMs
81	  the whole card and takes down its neighbours.
82	- **MIG needs a datacenter GPU** (A100/A30/H100…); GeForce/RTX cards can't do it.
83	- **`--mem` is a hard cap under cgroups, not a hint.** A job that needs more
84	  gets OOM-killed; bump `--mem`, don't expect bursting into idle RAM.
85	- **`sacct` needs accounting (`slurmdbd`) configured.** Without it use
86	  `scontrol show job <id>` (live only — gone after the job ages out).
87	- **A failing site `Prolog`/`Epilog` drains the node**, showing jobs as
88	  `PENDING` with a node `Reason=`. Check `scontrol show node`.
89	- **`srun --oversubscribe` is ignored under consumable resources** — you can't
90	  opportunistically grab more than you requested.
91
```

## 1. `skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`

Path: `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`

Top-level shape: `{ name, owner{name,email}, metadata{description,version}, plugins[] }`. The catalog is organized as an array of **plugin groups**, each bundling one or more skills. There are 13 plugin groups currently.

Each plugin entry has exactly these fields (verified consistent across all 13):
- `name` (string, kebab-case group id)
- `description` (string)
- `category` (string — free-form label; existing values: `Authoring`, `Workflow`, `Quality`, `ML`, `Notebooks`, `Web`, `Engineering`, `Research`, `Infra`)
- `tags` (string array)
- `source` (always `"./"`)
- `strict` (always `false`)
- `skills` (string array of paths **relative to `skills/`**, in `./local/<name>` or `./vendor/<name>` form — note the leading `./`, and vendored series use a nested `./vendor/<series>/<name>` form, e.g. `./vendor/fullstack-nextjs/nextjs`)

Exact JSON shape of one plugin entry (the `github-workflow` group, the closest existing analog):

```json

  "name": "github-workflow",
  "description": "Warp Oz skills for GitHub workflow automation: CI diagnosis & fix, PR creation, bug report triage, and duplicate issue detection",
  "category": "Engineering",
  "tags": ["github", "ci", "pull-request", "triage", "issues"],

}

**Where a `git-workflow` skill would fit** (reporting existing relevant groups, not proposing a design):
- There is already a `github-workflow` group (category `Engineering`, all `./vendor/*` skills from `warpdotdev/oz-skills`) — GitHub-platform-focused (CI, PRs, issue triage).
- There is an `engineering-fundamentals` group (category `Engineering`, all vendored mattpocock skills).
- No existing group is dedicated to local/plumbing git operations (commit/branch/worktree). A new local skill would be added as `"./local/git-workflow"` inside whichever group is chosen; there is no group whose skills are all local + git-plumbing-oriented today.

Here is the complete structure-and-conventions report for authoring `git-workflow` in this repo. All paths are absolute.

---

## 1. The templates under `skills/local/skill-author/assets/`

### `SKILL.md.template`
Frontmatter is exactly two fields, YAML between `---` fences:
```
---
name: SKILL_NAME_PLACEHOLDER
description: SKILL_DESCRIPTION_PLACEHOLDER (replace this — include "Use when..." with at least 3 concrete trigger contexts; target 120-500 chars and never exceed 1024.)
---
```
Body section order (headings verbatim):
1. `# SKILL_TITLE_PLACEHOLDER` — then a one-paragraph overview.
2. `## When to use` — bulleted concrete trigger phrases.
3. `## When NOT to use` — adjacent tasks that should route elsewhere.
4. `## Workflow` — numbered `### 1. Step` / `### 2. Step` subsections; imperative, explain *why*, fenced command blocks.
5. `## Available scripts` — "(Delete this section if the skill has no `scripts/`.)"; bullet per script with a nested `Flags:` line.
6. `## Bundled assets` — delete if no `assets/`; bullet `assets/x.template — when it's used`.
7. `## Reference files` — delete if no `references/`; bullet `references/x.md — Read this **when** [load condition]`.
8. `## Gotchas` — **explicitly must NOT be deleted**; empty is a yellow flag.

### `reference.md.template`
No frontmatter. Structure: `# REFERENCE_TITLE_PLACEHOLDER`, a one-paragraph summary that repeats the load condition ("Read this when…") for self-containment, a `## Table of contents` numbered anchor list, a `---` divider, then `## Section` headings.

### `script-bash.template`
`#!/usr/bin/env bash`; header comment states "Bash 3.2 compatible (works on stock macOS)"; `set -euo pipefail`; a `usage()` heredoc with `Usage:` / `Options:` (`--dry-run`, `--help, -h`) / `Examples:` / `Exit codes:` (0 success, 1 invalid args, 2 missing input); logging helpers `log/warn/die` all writing to **stderr**; a `while`/`case` arg-parse loop supporting `--`, unknown-flag `die`, positional collection; a `main()` that honors `--dry-run` and emits **structured JSON on stdout**.

### `script-python.template`
Shebang `#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script` with a PEP 723 `# /// script` inline-metadata block (`requires-python = ">=3.11"`, `dependencies = [...]`). Module docstring with run instructions and exit codes (0/1/2/3). Uses `argparse` via a `make_parser()`, a `log()` that prints to **stderr**, `main(argv)` returning int, `--dry-run` flag, JSON to stdout, `sys.exit(main())`.

---

## 2. Authoring rules (from the two reference files)

From `skills/local/skill-author/references/authoring-patterns.md`:
- **Description budget:** 120–500 chars preferred (Green), 501–900 Yellow, 901–1024 Orange, >1024 invalid (Red). First 60 chars must be meaningful (picker truncation). Include *what it does* + concrete "Use when X, Y, Z" triggers (≥3).
- **Progressive disclosure:** frontmatter always loaded; `SKILL.md` body <500 lines / <5000 tokens; `references/`, `assets/`, `scripts/` load on demand. Move overflow into `references/<topic>.md` and cite with a **load condition** ("Read X when Y"), never a bare "see X".
- **Name:** lowercase letters/digits/hyphens, no leading/trailing hyphen, no `--`, ≤64 chars.
- **Calibrated specificity:** be prescriptive only for destructive/ordered/exact-format ops — and even then **explain *why*** (no bare caps "MUST/ALWAYS/NEVER" without a reason). Give freedom for judgment-driven work.
- **Defaults, not menus:** pick one default tool + one escape hatch; don't enumerate every option.
- **Procedures over declarations:** teach the general approach, not the one-instance answer.
- **Gotchas section:** often the highest-value section; concrete corrections to mistakes the agent makes by default; keep it in `SKILL.md` (not a reference) so it's read *before* the trap; grow it from real runs.
- **Output templates:** paste the literal shape when output is structured; long/conditional templates go to `assets/<name>.template`.
- **Checklists** with `- [ ]` and dependency arrows for multi-step flows; **validation loops** (do→validate→fix→re-validate→proceed); **plan-validate-execute** for destructive/batch ops.
- **Bundle a script** when the agent reinvents the same ~20-line helper across 2+ runs.
- Ends with a "Quick checklist before commit."

From `skills/local/skill-author/references/this-repo-conventions.md`:
- **New skills go in `skills/local/<name>/`** with `SKILL.md` + `references/` + `scripts/` + `assets/`. Never hand-edit `skills/vendor/`.
- `.agents/skills/` and `.claude/skills/` at repo root are **relative symlink farms** (`../../skills/local/<name>`) created by `scripts/new-skill.sh`; never put canonical content there.
- Skill discovery: works because skills sit 2 levels deep; don't nest >5 levels.
- **All bundled scripts must be bash 3.2 compatible** (stock macOS). Bash for orchestration; PEP 723 Python allowed for parsing/analytical helpers.
- Some scripts are **mirrored byte-identical** to repo-root `scripts/`; keep in sync manually.
- Descriptions in this repo lean **even pushier** than agentskills.io guidance (OpenCode/Claude Code under-trigger). This file wins over agentskills.io on conflict.
- When adding a local skill also add: a row in `docs/skills/index.md`, a `docs/skills/<name>.md` page, a `mkdocs.yml` nav entry, and a README "What's in here" row. `AGENTS.md` is a symlink to `CLAUDE.md`.

## 3. The `agent-history-hygiene` skill (integration target)

Canonical path: `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/` (the copies under `site/` are generated docs — ignore them). SKILL.md is 323 lines.

**What it does:** keeps agent chat transcripts + plan files committed alongside the code diff that produced them, without leaking secrets. Three core invariants: (1) never `.gitignore` transcripts/plans, (2) rotate at the provider before any git rewrite, (3) `git push --force` is never the fix for a leak.

**SKILL.md structure (non-standard, richer than the template):**
- Frontmatter: `name` + a long `description` (~900 chars, Yellow/Orange tier) packed with literal path globs (`.specstory/history/*.md`, `.claude/plans/*.md`, `.cursor/plans/`, etc.) and quoted user-utterance triggers ("commit my chat", "my .env leaked in chat", "bootstrap pre-commit").
- Title + intro paragraph, then a **surface table** mapping each script/reference to "the question it answers."
- `## Core invariants` (numbered).
- `## When to use this skill` / `## When NOT to use` (both bilingual — includes Chinese trigger phrases).
- `## Integration with existing infrastructure` — describes how it layers on chezmoi's global `core.hooksPath`, `.gitleaks.toml`, and the pinned hook; then "What this skill adds."
- `## Workflow A: commit-time hygiene` / `## Workflow B: bootstrap a new project` / `## Workflow C: post-leak remediation` — each with fenced bash showing the exact `bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/<x>.sh` invocation.
- `## Gotchas` — very long, includes a full pitfall write-up (the active-SpecStory-writer redact loop).
- `## Available scripts` (each with full flag signature), `## Bundled assets`, `## Reference files` (each with load condition), `## Tests`, `## Related skills` (cross-links `project-knowledge-harness`).

**Scripts** (`scripts/`, all bash 3.2, `usage()` + structured exit codes):
- `find-session.sh [--format=specstory|claude|both] [--json]` — locate the current session's transcript/plan; always exits 0.
- `stage-agent-artifacts.sh [--session-only] [--include-all-plans] [--dry-run] [--allow-empty]` — `git add` the right artifacts; refuses if no code changes unless `--allow-empty`.

## 2. Authoring rules (from the two reference files)

From `skills/local/skill-author/references/authoring-patterns.md`:
- **Description budget:** 120–500 chars preferred (Green), 501–900 Yellow, 901–1024 Orange, &gt;1024 invalid (Red). First 60 chars must be meaningful (picker truncation). Include *what it does* + concrete "Use when X, Y, Z" triggers (≥3).
- **Progressive disclosure:** frontmatter always loaded; `SKILL.md` body &lt;500 lines / &lt;5000 tokens; `references/`, `assets/`, `scripts/` load on demand. Move overflow into `references/&lt;topic&gt;.md` and cite with a **load condition** ("Read X when Y"), never a bare "see X".
- **Name:** lowercase letters/digits/hyphens, no leading/trailing hyphen, no `--`, ≤64 chars.
- **Calibrated specificity:** be prescriptive only for destructive/ordered/exact-format ops — and even then **explain *why*** (no bare caps "MUST/ALWAYS/NEVER" without a reason). Give freedom for judgment-driven work.
- **Defaults, not menus:** pick one default tool + one escape hatch; don't enumerate every option.
- **Procedures over declarations:** teach the general approach, not the one-instance answer.
- **Gotchas section:** often the highest-value section; concrete corrections to mistakes the agent makes by default; keep it in `SKILL.md` (not a reference) so it's read *before* the trap; grow it from real runs.
- **Output templates:** paste the literal shape when output is structured; long/conditional templates go to `assets/&lt;name&gt;.template`.
- **Checklists** with `- [ ]` and dependency arrows for multi-step flows; **validation loops** (do→validate→fix→re-validate→proceed); **plan-validate-execute** for destructive/batch ops.
- **Bundle a script** when the agent reinvents the same ~20-line helper across 2+ runs.
- Ends with a "Quick checklist before commit."

From `skills/local/skill-author/references/this-repo-conventions.md`:
- **New skills go in `skills/local/&lt;name&gt;/`** with `SKILL.md` + `references/` + `scripts/` + `assets/`. Never hand-edit `skills/vendor/`.
- `.agents/skills/` and `.claude/skills/` at repo root are **relative symlink farms** (`../../skills/local/&lt;name&gt;`) created by `scripts/new-skill.sh`; never put canonical content there.
- Skill discovery: works because skills sit 2 levels deep; don't nest &gt;5 levels.
- **All bundled scripts must be bash 3.2 compatible** (stock macOS). Bash for orchestration; PEP 723 Python allowed for parsing/analytical helpers.
- Some scripts are **mirrored byte-identical** to repo-root `scripts/`; keep in sync manually.
- Descriptions in this repo lean **even pushier** than agentskills.io guidance (OpenCode/Claude Code under-trigger). This file wins over agentskills.io on conflict.

## docs/ structure and conventions for a `git-workflow` skill's educational docs

### 1. Top-level `docs/` structure

All under `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/docs/`:

| Dir / file | What lives there |
|---|---|
| `_snippets/` | Reusable include fragments (`domain-hub-template.md`, `external-install.md`, `install.md`). Pulled into pages via pymdownx snippets `--8<-- "..."`; never rendered as their own page (suppressed by `not_in_nav: /_snippets/` in mkdocs.yml). |
| `assets/copy-to-llm/` | CSS/JS for the "copy to LLM" button. Not content. |
| `catalog/` | The vendoring decision log + external-awareness wiki. Sub-dirs: `domains/` (per-domain hub pages), `mcp/` (MCP wiki, one file per server). Plus `catalog/index.md`, `catalog/skill-collections.md`. |
| `reference/` | Long-form, human-facing reference/spec docs (~14 topics). This is where "educational reference material" lives. Examples: `todo-format.md`, `tag-schema.md`, `llm-wiki-pattern.md`, `sdd-and-harnesses.md`, `deep-research-landscape.md`. |
| `skills/` | One human-facing page per skill (`docs/skills/<skill>.md`) — "should I use this?" companion to the agent-facing `SKILL.md`. |
| `workflows/` | Procedural how-to guides (4 topics: `adding-vendor-skills`, `creating-local-skills`, `adding-catalog-entries`, `project-memory`). |
| top-level pages | `index.md`, `getting-started.md`, `conventions.md`, `changelog.md`. |

`docs/conventions.md` (lines 44–54) is the governing rule for doc placement: every local skill gets a `docs/skills/<skill>.md` human page; long-form references that the agent loads on demand (`skills/local/<skill>/references/*.md`) "can be mirrored or summarized under `docs/reference/` when the audience extends to humans," but the canonical copy stays next to `SKILL.md`.

### 2. Format/style of representative files

Both files start directly with an H1 `#` heading — no YAML frontmatter. (Frontmatter is used only by `catalog/` pages, e.g. `docs/catalog/mcp/financialdatasets-ai.md` has `name/slug/upstream_url/transport/auth/hosting/domain` frontmatter. `workflows/` and `reference/` have none.)

- `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md` — 112 lines / ~4.3 KB. Procedural how-to: opening context paragraph, decision tables, bash code fences, a snippet include (`--8<-- "_snippets/external-install.md"`), relative markdown cross-links (`../catalog/index.md`), and a closing `## Validation` section with `make` commands. Second-person imperative voice.
- `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/docs/reference/todo-format.md` — 78 lines / ~3.1 KB. Reference/spec style: documents an exact grammar with tables, code-fence examples, and cross-links to other docs pages and to GitHub source. Reference files vary widely in length — from ~0.7 KB (`mkdocs-2-and-zensical.zh-TW.md`) up to ~18 KB (`sdd-and-harnesses.md`).

Common Material-for-MkDocs features available (from `markdown_extensions`): admonitions, `pymdownx.details`, tables, `def_list`, footnotes, tabbed blocks, mermaid via superfences, `toc.permalink`, and pymdownx snippets (base paths: `.`, `docs`, `docs/_snippets`).

### 3. Bilingual pattern — applies to ALL published pages, not just catalog

The quoted rule lives in `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/CLAUDE.md` line 228: "Every published catalog page is bilingual (`*.md` + `*.zh-TW.md`)." That sentence names catalog explicitly, but in practice the pattern covers every published nav page: there are 62 `*.zh-TW.md` files, and **every** file in `workflows/`, `reference/`, `skills/`, `catalog/` and the top-level pages has a matching `<name>.zh-TW.md` sibling (e.g. `docs/reference/todo-format.md` + `docs/reference/todo-format.zh-TW.md`; `docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md` + `.zh-TW.md`). Pattern is `<slug>.md` (English) + `<slug>.zh-TW.md` (繁體中文) side-by-side in the same directory.

Mechanism: the `i18n` plugin in mkdocs.yml (`docs_structure: suffix`, locales `en` default + `zh-TW`, `fallback_to_default: true`). Because of `fallback_to_default`, a missing translation does not break the build — so bilingual is a **convention enforced in-PR, not by the build**. The `workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md` "Bilingual obligation" section (lines 94–100) states the same: both languages should ship in the same PR.

So: a new `docs/reference/git-workflow.md` educational doc would conventionally need a `docs/reference/git-workflow.zh-TW.md` counterpart.

### 4. mkdocs.yml nav — manual, requires editing

`/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/mkdocs.yml` — the `nav:` block (lines 99–170) is a **hand-maintained explicit list**; each page is registered by path under a titled section. Relevant sections:
- `Workflows:` (lines 103–107) — each workflow file listed by title.
- `Reference:` (lines 155–169) — each reference page listed by title, e.g. `- TODO format: reference/todo-format.md`.

Adding a new doc **does require editing this nav** (there is no awesome-pages/auto-nav plugin). You add only the English `.md` path — the zh-TW sibling is auto-derived by the i18n `suffix` structure into the language switcher, so zh-TW files are NOT listed separately in nav.

Two other registration surfaces to note:
- The `llmstxt` plugin (lines 47–68) has its own `sections:` using **globs** (`workflows/*.md`, `reference/*.md`, `skills/*.md`, `catalog/*.md`, etc.), so new files are auto-picked into `llms.txt`/`llms-full.txt` with no editing.
- `validation.links.not_found: info` (lines 188–190) keeps `--strict` builds passing while still surfacing broken links; `make docs-build` runs strict mode.

### 5. Existing git-related documentation

There is **no dedicated git / commit / branch / worktree / semver / conventional-commits doc anywhere in `docs/`** — no file is named for those topics, and no reference/workflow page covers general git best practices. The broad grep hits earlier were almost all `github.com` URLs, not git-topic content. The only substantive in-body mentions:

- `docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md` (line 193) — "semver-style" version numbers, in passing.

Tangentially related but not git-best-practices: the `agent-history-hygiene` skill (`docs/skills/agent-history-hygiene.md` + `.zh-TW.md`, and `skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/`) deals with committing coding-agent artifacts without leaking secrets — adjacent territory, but not a general git-workflow reference.

Net: a git best-practices "科普" doc would be greenfield. Based on `conventions.md`, the fit is `docs/reference/git-workflow.md` (+ `.zh-TW.md`) for the human-facing educational copy, registered under the `Reference:` nav section, with the canonical agent-facing copy living next to the skill's `SKILL.md` (e.g. `skills/local/git-workflow/references/`). 117	# 4. Commit. pre-commit (installed by bootstrap) runs redact-agent-secrets
118	#    then gitleaks again as a catch-all.
119	git commit -m "feat: ..."
120	```
121	
122	## Workflow B: bootstrap a new project
123	
124	For repos that don't yet have `.pre-commit-config.yaml` / `.gitleaks.toml`
125	installed. Runs once per repo.
126	
127	```bash
128	cd /path/to/new/project
129	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/bootstrap-project.sh \
130	  --install-hook            # optional: auto-stage on every commit
131	
132	# Verify: shake out any existing issues in the working tree.
133	pre-commit run --all-files
134	```
135	
136	What `bootstrap-project.sh` does:
137	
138	1. Drops `.pre-commit-config.yaml` + `.gitleaks.toml` into the repo
139	   (skips if already present unless `--force`). The redactor is a pinned
140	   remote hook (`repo: …/agent-skills`, `rev: ahh-v1.1.0`), **not** a
141	   vendored `scripts/redact_secrets.py` — so `pre-commit autoupdate`
142	   keeps it current everywhere.
143	2. Runs `pre-commit install` (or `uvx pre-commit@4 install` if
144	   pre-commit isn't on `PATH`).
145	3. Audits `.gitignore` / `.git/info/exclude` for patterns that would
146	   silently hide an agent artifact dir — warns without editing.
147	4. Checks `~/.claude/settings.json` for `plansDirectory`; prints the
148	   one-line patch if missing.
149	5. With `--install-hook`: writes a `prepare-commit-msg` hook that calls
150	   `stage-agent-artifacts.sh --session-only --allow-empty` so every
151	   `git commit` auto-attaches the current session file.
152	
153	Migrating a repo off the **old vendored layout** (a committed
154	`scripts/redact_secrets.py` + a `- repo: local` redact hook):
155	
156	```bash
157	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/scripts/bootstrap-project.sh --migrate
158	```
159	
160	removes the vendored script and rewrites the local hook into the pinned
161	remote hook, leaving your other hooks and `.gitleaks.toml` untouched
162	(idempotent; safe to re-run).
163	
164	## Workflow C: post-leak remediation
165	
166	When `scan-staged.sh` reports exit `10`/`20`, or the user says "I
167	committed / pushed a secret":
168	
169	1. **STOP** the user from running `git push --force` reflexively.
170	2. Read `references/remediation.md` end-to-end.
171	3. Walk the user through **step 1 (rotate)** regardless of blast
172	   radius. Only after rotation does the question of scrubbing history
173	   become worth discussing.
174	4. Use the decision tree in the runbook to pick the right git action.
175	
176	## Gotchas
177	
178	- **`plansDirectory` project-level sometimes ignored.** Claude Code
179	  issue [#19537](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/19537)
180	  reports project-level `plansDirectory` being ignored in some
181	  versions. After running a `/plan`, verify the file actually landed
182	  where you expected before relying on `stage-agent-artifacts.sh`
183	  picking it up. User-level config (`~/.claude/settings.json` with
184	  `"plansDirectory": "./.claude/plans"`) is the recommended default.
185	- **`gitleaks protect` is deprecated.** Since v8.19.0 use
186	  `gitleaks git --staged --redact` (pre-commit) and
187	  `gitleaks dir <path>` (working directory). The older commands still
188	  work but emit a deprecation notice. This skill uses the modern
189	  syntax everywhere.
190	- **`pre-commit install` is per-clone.** Each teammate must run
191	  `pre-commit install` in their own clone for hooks to fire. CI cannot
192	  be trusted as the single gate — it's second-chance, not last-chance.
193	- **Transcript files can be huge.** A long SpecStory session can exceed
194	  2 MB. The template bumps `check-added-large-files` to `--maxkb=2048`
195	  to avoid false positives, but a very long session can still overflow.
196	  If you hit the limit, rotate sessions (`specstory run claude`
197	  creates a fresh file) instead of raising the cap further.
198	- **Session-UUID divergence between SpecStory CLI and VS Code
199	  extension.** The extension autosaves into `.specstory/history/`
200	  continuously; the CLI (`specstory run claude`) creates one file per
201	  invocation. If both are active you can end up with two transcripts
202	  for what feels like "one session" — mtime-newest wins in
203	  `find-session.sh`.
204	- **Global `core.hooksPath` means bare repos aren't protected.** The
205	  chezmoi setup's global hook runs `.pre-commit-config.yaml` IF it
206	  exists — so a repo without `.pre-commit-config.yaml` has no
207	  protection. Run `bootstrap-project.sh` before the first commit with
208	  agent artifacts, not after.
209	- **Active SpecStory writer can defeat the redact loop.** The standard
210	  `git add → git commit → pre-commit auto-fixes → re-stage → re-commit`
211	  flow assumes the file is **quiescent** during the commit. SpecStory's
212	  `specstory_*_watch` daemon tails the agent transcript continuously,
213	  so if the chat captured `ps -axo args`-style output that contained an
214	  unrelated daemon's secret in argv (e.g. SpecStory's own
215	  `--cloud-token …` flag), every diagnostic command (`grep`, `sed -n
216	  '<line>p'`, `cat | head | tail`) prints the secret again, SpecStory
217	  appends it to the transcript, and the redact-then-restage cycle
218	  never converges. Symptom: pre-commit says "Successfully redacted N
219	  file(s)" but `gitleaks-system` immediately fails on the same line,
220	  re-running `git add && git commit` doesn't help, and `grep -c
221	  '<secret-prefix>' file` shows the count *increasing* over commit
222	  attempts. **Workaround**: a single atomic
223	  `python3 -c "<in-place re.sub>" && git add <file> && git commit -m
224	  "..."` pipeline so the index is frozen before any new specstory write
225	  lands. **Don't** print, grep, or diff the secret line during the
226	  recovery — every print echoes back into the transcript. Diagnose with
227	  `lsof <file>` (looking for `specstory_*` writers) instead. See
228	  `pitfalls/redact-secrets-loop-with-active-specstory-writer.md` in
229	  upstream chezmoi for the full debugging trail.
230	  **Fixed sub-case:** the *bare-phrase* variant of this loop — where the
231	  redactor's own `PRIVATE KEY` substring match kept flagging prose that
232	  merely *discusses* private keys (this skill's docs, or a chat about
233	  redaction) with **no real secret present** — no longer happens.
234	  `redact_secrets.py` now scopes to key *headers* (the
235	  `detect-private-key` BLACKLIST), so prose mentions are ignored and
236	  converge immediately. The atomic-commit workaround above is still
237	  needed for the harder case: a **real** secret an active writer keeps
238	  re-appending. When only the substring redactor (`redact-agent-secrets`)
239	  trips while `gitleaks` + `detect-private-key` pass, it's the false
240	  positive — verify with `gitleaks git --staged` and, if clean, commit
241	  with `SKIP=redact-agent-secrets` (keeps the real gates active).
242	
243	## Available scripts
244	
245	- **`scripts/find-session.sh [--format=specstory|claude|both] [--json]`**
246	  Discover the current agent session files for `$PWD`. TSV default,
247	  `--json` for structured callers. Never exits non-zero (always 0,
248	  empty fields signal absence).
249	
250	- **`scripts/stage-agent-artifacts.sh [--session-only] [--include-all-plans] [--dry-run] [--allow-empty]`**
251	  `git add` the right agent artifacts before the next commit.
252	  `--session-only` stages only the current SpecStory + newest plan;
253	  default stages every dirty `*.md` in every configured artifact dir.
254	  Refuses to run if there are no code changes (prevents "commit just
255	  transcript"); override with `--allow-empty`.
256	
257	- **`scripts/scan-staged.sh [--redact] [--verbose]`**
258	  Run `gitleaks git --staged` with agent-friendly exit codes
259	  (0 clean / 10 redacted / 20 leaks / 30 gitleaks missing). JSON lines
260	  on stdout, prose diagnostics on stderr.
261	
262	- **`scripts/bootstrap-project.sh [--from-chezmoi] [--install-hook] [--force] [--dry-run]`**
263	  Install `.pre-commit-config.yaml` + `.gitleaks.toml` + the redactor
264	  into the current repo, then run `pre-commit install`. Audits
265	  `.gitignore` and `~/.claude/settings.json` for misconfigurations
266	  (warns, never silently edits).
267	
268	## Bundled assets
269	
270	- `assets/artifact-dirs.txt` — the canonical list of agent artifact
271	  directories (SpecStory, Claude plans, Cursor plans + rules, OpenCode
272	  plans, Spec-kit, Codex). Consumed by `stage-agent-artifacts.sh` and
273	  by `bootstrap-project.sh` when rendering the pre-commit `files:`
274	  regex.
275	- `assets/pre-commit-config.yaml.template` — minimal
276	  `.pre-commit-config.yaml` with `redact-agent-secrets` + gitleaks +
277	  standard hygiene hooks.
278	- `assets/gitleaks.toml.template` — portable subset of the chezmoi
279	  `.gitleaks.toml` with custom rule IDs + a path-scoped allowlist for
280	  agent artifact dirs.
281	- `assets/redact_secrets.py` — bundled copy of chezmoi's
282	  `scripts/redact_secrets.py`. Chezmoi version is upstream; sync doc
283	  in `references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`.
284	
285	## Reference files
286	
287	- [`references/transcript-session-discovery.md`](references/transcript-session-discovery.md)
288	  — SpecStory / Claude session layouts and the `$PWD → slug` algorithm.
289	  Read when `find-session.sh` returns empty or ambiguous results.
290	- [`references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md`](references/pre-commit-redaction-stack.md)
291	  — three-layer defense (redact → gitleaks → `scan-staged.sh`),
292	  allowlist design, sync procedure for the bundled redactor. Read
293	  when tuning rules or debugging unexpected pre-commit failures.
294	- [`references/remediation.md`](references/remediation.md) —
295	  rotate-first runbook for "I committed / pushed a secret". Read
296	  **before** any `git filter-repo` / `git push --force` action.
297	
298	## Tests
299	
300	The skill ships with a three-level test suite under
301	[`tests/`](tests/README.md). Run from repo root:
302	
303	```bash
304	make test-skill
305	```
306	
307	- `test_redact_secrets.py` — pytest for pure redactor functions.
308	- `test_gitleaks_corpus.py` — golden-corpus fixtures staged in tmp git
309	  repos, asserting real-key shapes fire and example shapes are
310	  allowlisted only inside configured artifact dirs.
311	- `test_scan_staged.sh` — exit-code contract for
312	  `scripts/scan-staged.sh` (0 / 20 / 30 / 2).
313	
314	The corpus + shell tests skip gracefully when `gitleaks` isn't on
315	`PATH`. See [`tests/README.md`](tests/README.md) for what each
316	regression the suite locks in.
317

```text
> ## Documentation Index
> Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://code.claude.com/docs/llms.txt
> Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Run parallel sessions with worktrees

> Isolate parallel Claude Code sessions in separate git worktrees so changes don't collide. Covers the `--worktree` flag, subagent isolation, `.worktreeinclude`, cleanup, and non-git VCS hooks.

A [git worktree](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree) is a separate working directory with its own files and branch, sharing the same repository history and remote as your main checkout. Running each Claude Code session in its own worktree means edits in one session never touch files in another, so you can have Claude building a feature in one terminal while fixing a bug in a second.

This page covers worktree isolation in the CLI. Everything below assumes a git repository. For other version control systems, see [Non-git version control](#non-git-version-control). The [desktop app](/en/desktop#work-in-parallel-with-sessions) creates a worktree for every new session automatically.

Worktrees are one of several ways to run Claude in parallel. They isolate file edits, while [subagents](/en/sub-agents) and [agent teams](/en/agent-teams) coordinate the work itself. See [Run agents in parallel](/en/agents) to compare the approaches, or skip ahead to [Isolate subagents with worktrees](#isolate-subagents-with-worktrees) to use worktrees and subagents together.

## Start Claude in a worktree

Pass `--worktree` or `-w` to create an isolated worktree and start Claude in it. By default, the worktree is created under `.claude/worktrees/<value>/` at your repository root, on a new branch named `worktree-<value>`:

```bash theme={null}
claude --worktree feature-auth
```

To put worktrees somewhere else, configure a [`WorktreeCreate` hook](#non-git-version-control). Run the command again with a different name in another terminal to start a second isolated session:

```bash theme={null}
claude --worktree bugfix-123
```

If you omit the name, Claude generates one such as `bright-running-fox`:

```bash theme={null}
claude --worktree
```

You can also ask Claude to "work in a worktree" during a session, and it will create one with the [`EnterWorktree`](/en/tools-reference) tool. Once in a worktree, Claude can switch directly to another one under `.claude/worktrees/` by calling `EnterWorktree` with the target path. The previous worktree stays on disk untouched.

Entering a path outside the repository's `.claude/worktrees/` directory asks for your approval first, because it moves the session's working directory, write access, and project configuration such as `CLAUDE.md` and settings to that location. An `EnterWorktree` [permission rule](/en/permissions) or choosing "don't ask again" doesn't suppress this prompt; only `bypassPermissions` mode skips it. Before v2.1.206, Claude could enter any existing worktree path without asking.

{/* min-version: 2.1.198 */}As of v2.1.198, entering or exiting a worktree also relocates the session transcript to that directory's project storage, the same way [`/cd`](/en/commands) does, so `/desktop` and `--resume` find the session there afterward. Worktrees created by a [`WorktreeCreate` hook](#non-git-version-control) are excluded and keep the transcript at the launch directory.

Before using `--worktree` interactively in a directory for the first time, accept the workspace trust dialog by running `claude` once in that directory. If trust has not yet been accepted, `--worktree` exits with an error and prompts you to run `claude` in the directory first. Non-interactive runs with `-p` skip the [trust check](/en/security), so `claude -p --worktree` proceeds without it.

If Claude Code can't enter the worktree directory at startup, for example because a [`WorktreeCreate` hook](/en/hooks#worktreecreate) printed something other than the directory it created, or because the directory was deleted after it was set up, Claude Code prints an error naming the path and exits with code 1. Before v2.1.205, this crashed the session, and with `-p` it stalled for about 30 seconds before exiting with code 0.

{/* min-version: 2.1.200 */}Plugins installed at [project scope](/en/plugins-reference#plugin-installation-scopes) from the main checkout also load in worktrees of the same repository, so you don't need to reinstall them per worktree. This applies whether you create the worktree with `--worktree` or with `git worktree add`. Requires Claude Code v2.1.200 or later.

<Tip>
  Add `.claude/worktrees/` to your `.gitignore` so worktree contents don't appear as untracked files in your main checkout.
</Tip>

### Choose the base branch

Worktrees branch from your repository's default branch, `origin/HEAD`, so they start from a clean tree matching the remote. When nothing has fetched the repository in the last 24 hours, Claude Code refreshes `origin/HEAD` with a fetch of the default branch, capped at five seconds, and uses the locally cached ref if the fetch fails. If no remote is configured, or `origin/HEAD` isn't cached locally and can't be fetched, the worktree falls back to your current local `HEAD`.

The refresh requires Claude Code v2.1.208 or later; before that, a fresh worktree used whatever `origin/HEAD` was already cached locally.

To always branch from local `HEAD` instead, set `worktree.baseRef` to `"head"` in [settings](/en/settings#worktree-settings). Setting `baseRef` to `"head"` makes new worktrees carry your unpushed commits and feature-branch state, which is useful when isolating subagents that need to operate on in-progress work. The setting accepts only `"fresh"` or `"head"`, not arbitrary git refs:

```json theme={null}
{
  "worktree": {
    "baseRef": "head"
  }
}
```

To branch from a specific pull request, pass the PR number prefixed with `#`, or a full GitHub pull request URL. Claude Code fetches `pull/<number>/head` from `origin` and creates the worktree at `.claude/worktrees/pr-<number>`:

```bash theme={null}
claude --worktree "#1234"
```

For full control over how worktrees are created, configure a [`WorktreeCreate` hook](/en/hooks#worktreecreate), which replaces the default `git worktree` logic entirely.

### Reuse a worktree name

Reusing a worktree name whose directory already exists resumes that worktree.

A resumed worktree resets to the [current base](#choose-the-base-branch) instead of resuming at its old tip when all of the following hold:

* It has no uncommitted changes or untracked files.
* It is still on the branch Claude Code created for it.
* It never committed, or its pull request was merged and its remote branch deleted.

Before v2.1.208, a reused name always resumed the old worktree at its old tip.

## Copy gitignored files into worktrees

A worktree is a fresh checkout, so untracked files like `.env` or `.env.local` from your main repository are not present. To copy them automatically when Claude creates a worktree, add a `.worktreeinclude` file to your project root.

The file uses `.gitignore` syntax. Only files that match a pattern and are also gitignored are copied, so tracked files are never duplicated.

This `.worktreeinclude` copies two env files and a secrets config into each new worktree:

```text .worktreeinclude theme={null}
.env
.env.local
config/secrets.json
```

This applies to worktrees created with `--worktree`, [subagent worktrees](#isolate-subagents-with-worktrees), and parallel sessions in the [desktop app](/en/desktop#work-in-parallel-with-sessions).

## Isolate subagents with worktrees

Subagents can run in their own worktrees so parallel edits don't conflict. Ask Claude to "use worktrees for your agents", or set it permanently on a [custom subagent](/en/sub-agents#supported-frontmatter-fields) by adding `isolation: worktree` to the frontmatter. Each subagent gets a temporary worktree that is removed automatically when the subagent finishes without changes.

Subagent worktrees use the same [base branch](#choose-the-base-branch) as `--worktree`, so they branch from your repository's default branch unless `worktree.baseRef` is set to `"head"`.

## Clean up worktrees

When you exit a worktree session, cleanup depends on whether you made changes:

* **No uncommitted changes, no untracked files, and no new commits**: the worktree and its branch are removed automatically. If the session has a [name](/en/sessions#name-your-sessions), Claude prompts instead so you can keep the worktree for later
* **Uncommitted changes, untracked files, or new commits exist**: Claude prompts you to keep or remove the worktree. Keeping preserves the directory and branch so you can return later. Removing deletes the worktree directory and its branch, discarding any uncommitted changes, untracked files, and commits
* **Non-interactive runs**: worktrees created with `--worktree` alongside `-p` are not cleaned up automatically since there is no exit prompt. Remove them with `git worktree remove`

Worktrees that Claude created for subagents and [background sessions](/en/agent-view#how-file-edits-are-isolated) are removed automatically once they are older than your [`cleanupPeriodDays`](/en/settings#available-settings) setting, provided they have no uncommitted changes, no untracked files, and no unpushed commits. Worktrees you create with `--worktree` are never removed by this sweep.

While an agent is running, Claude runs `git worktree lock` on its worktree so that concurrent cleanup cannot remove it. The lock is released when the agent finishes. To clean up a worktree that the sweep keeps, run `git worktree remove`, adding `--force` if the worktree has uncommitted changes or untracked files.

On Windows, before removing a worktree, Claude Code removes any NTFS junction or directory symlink at any depth inside it as a link entry, so removing the worktree doesn't delete the files a link points to. Before v2.1.205, Claude Code removed only top-level links as link entries, and removing a worktree with a junction nested in a subdirectory could delete the contents of the directory the link pointed to outside the worktree.

## Manage worktrees manually

For full control over worktree location and branch configuration, create worktrees with Git directly. This is useful when you need to check out a specific existing branch or place the worktree outside the repository.

Create a worktree on a new branch:

```bash theme={null}
git worktree add ../project-feature-a -b feature-a
```

Create a worktree from an existing branch:

```bash theme={null}
git worktree add ../project-bugfix bugfix-123
```

Start Claude in the worktree:

```bash theme={null}
cd ../project-feature-a && claude
```

List your worktrees:

```bash theme={null}
git worktree list
```

Remove one when you're done with it:

```bash theme={null}
git worktree remove ../project-feature-a
```

See the [Git worktree documentation](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree) for the full command reference. Remember to initialize your development environment in each new worktree: install dependencies, set up virtual environments, or run whatever your project's setup requires.

## Non-git version control

Worktree isolation uses git by default. For SVN, Perforce, Mercurial, or other systems, configure [`WorktreeCreate` and `WorktreeRemove` hooks](/en/hooks#worktreecreate) to provide custom creation and cleanup logic. Because the hook replaces the default git behavior, [`.worktreeinclude`](#copy-gitignored-files-into-worktrees) is not processed when you use `--worktree`. Copy any local configuration files inside your hook script instead.

This `WorktreeCreate` hook reads the worktree name from stdin, checks out a fresh SVN working copy, and prints the directory path so Claude Code can use it as the session's working directory:

```json theme={null}
{
  "hooks": {
    "WorktreeCreate": [
      {
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "bash -c 'NAME=$(jq -r .name); DIR=\"$HOME/.claude/worktrees/$NAME\"; svn checkout https://svn.example.com/repo/trunk \"$DIR\" >&2 && echo \"$DIR\"'"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Pair it with a `WorktreeRemove` hook to clean up when the session ends. See the [hooks reference](/en/hooks#worktreecreate) for the input schema and a removal example.

## See also

Worktrees handle file isolation. The related pages below cover delegating work into those isolated checkouts and switching between the sessions you create:

* [Subagents](/en/sub-agents): delegate work to isolated agents within a session
* [Agent teams](/en/agent-teams): coordinate multiple Claude sessions automatically
* [Manage sessions](/en/sessions): name, resume, and switch between conversations
* [Desktop parallel sessions](/en/desktop#work-in-parallel-with-sessions): worktree-backed sessions in the desktop app
```
</details></tool-use>
